title.zh: 卷三百六十七 列傳第一百二十六 李顯忠 楊存中 郭浩 楊政
title.en: Volume 367 Biographies 126: Li Xianzhong, Yang Cunzhong, Guo Hao, Yang Zheng
title.raw: 卷三百六十七 列傳第一百二十六 李顯忠 楊存中 郭浩 楊政 Volume 367 Biographies 126: Li Xianzhong, Yang Cunzhong, Guo Hao, Yang Zheng

sentences.zh: 李顯忠 楊存中 郭浩 楊政

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong, Yang Cunzhong, Guo Hao, Yang Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong, Yang Cunzhong, Guo Hao, and Yang Zheng

sentences.zh: 李顯忠

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong

sentences.zh: 李顯忠，綏德軍青澗人也。

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong was a native of Qingjian in Suide Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong was a native of Qingjian in Suide Army.

sentences.zh: 初名世輔，南歸，賜名顯忠。

translations.literal: His original name was Shifu; after he defected to the south he was granted the name Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Shifu, he received the name Xianzhong when he came over to the Song.

sentences.zh: 由唐以來，世襲蘇尾九族巡檢。

translations.literal: From the Tang dynasty onward his family had hereditarily held the post of Xunjian of the Nine Clans of Suwei.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang, his family had held the hereditary post of inspector over the nine clans of Suwei.

sentences.zh: 初，其母當產，數日不能免，有僧過門曰：「所孕乃奇男子，當以劍、矢置母旁，即生。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when his mother was due to give birth she could not deliver for several days; a monk passing the door said, "What you carry is an extraordinary boy—place a sword and arrows beside the mother and he will be born."
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was in labor she could not deliver for days; a monk at the door said, "You carry an extraordinary son—set a sword and arrows beside her and he will be born."

sentences.zh: 已而果生顯忠，立於蓐，鹹異之。

translations.literal: Soon after Xianzhong was indeed born; he stood upright on the birthing mat, and all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was born as foretold and stood upright on the birthing mat—a marvel to everyone.

sentences.zh: 年十七，投效用，隨父永奇出入行陣。

translations.literal: At seventeen he entered military service and followed his father Yongqi in and out of battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he enlisted and followed his father Yongqi through the ranks in campaign.

sentences.zh: 金人犯鄜延，經略王庶命永奇募間者，得張琦；

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded Fuyan, the pacification commissioner Wang Shu ordered Yongqi to recruit agents and obtained Zhang Qi;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded Fuyan, Pacification Commissioner Wang Shu had Yongqi recruit scouts and found Zhang Qi;

sentences.zh: 更求一人，顯忠請行。

translations.literal: when one more man was sought, Xianzhong asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: when a second man was needed, Xianzhong volunteered.

sentences.zh: 永奇曰：「汝未涉曆，行必累琦。」

translations.literal: Yongqi said, "You lack experience; if you go you will surely burden Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Yongqi said, "You have no experience—you will only hold Qi back."

sentences.zh: 顯忠曰：「顯忠年小，膽氣不小，必不累琦，當與琦俱。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong said, "Xianzhong is young but his courage is not small; he will surely not burden Qi and ought to go with him."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong replied, "I may be young, but my nerve is not—I will not burden Qi. I am going with him."

sentences.zh: 有敵人夜宿陶穴，顯忠縋穴中，得十七人，皆殺之，取首二級，馬二匹，余馬悉折其足。

translations.literal: Some enemies were lodging at night in pottery caves; Xianzhong lowered himself into a cave, seized seventeen men, and killed them all, taking two heads and two horses and breaking the legs of all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies were bivouacked in pottery caves; Xianzhong lowered himself in, killed all seventeen, took two heads and two horses, and lamed every other mount.

sentences.zh: 庶大奇之，補承信郎，充隊將，由是始知名。

translations.literal: Wang Shu was greatly astonished and appointed him Chengxin Lang, assigning him as a platoon leader; from this he first became known.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was astonished, appointed him Chengxin Lang as platoon leader, and his name began to spread.

sentences.zh: 轉武翼郎，充副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wuyi Lang and served as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Wuyi Lang and made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 金人陷延安，授顯忠父子官。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens took Yan'an they conferred offices on Xianzhong and his father.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin captured Yan'an they gave father and son official posts.

sentences.zh: 永奇聚泣曰：「我宋臣也，世襲國恩，乃為彼用邪！」

translations.literal: Yongqi gathered his family and wept, saying, "We are subjects of Song, who have received the state's favor for generations—shall we now serve them!"
translations.idiomatic: Yongqi gathered his kin and wept: "We are Song subjects who have enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations—shall we serve the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 會劉豫令顯忠帥馬軍赴東京，永奇密戒之曰：「汝若得乘機，即歸本朝，無以我故貳其志。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu ordered Xianzhong to lead the horse army to the Eastern Capital, Yongqi secretly admonished him: "If you seize an opportunity, return at once to our dynasty; do not let concern for me make you waver in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu sent Xianzhong to lead cavalry to the Eastern Capital, Yongqi secretly urged him: "If you see your chance, return to the Song—do not let loyalty to me weaken your resolve.

sentences.zh: 事成，我亦不朽矣。」

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, I too shall be imperishable."
translations.idiomatic: If you succeed, I too will live on in honor."

sentences.zh: 顯忠至東京，劉麟喜之，授南路鈐轄，乃密遣其客雷燦以蠟書赴行在。

translations.literal: Xianzhong reached the Eastern Capital; Liu Lin was pleased with him and appointed him Southern Route Qianxia, and he secretly sent his retainer Lei Can with a wax-sealed letter to the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital Liu Lin favored him and made him Southern Route Qianxia; he secretly sent his client Lei Can with a wax-sealed letter to the court.

sentences.zh: 已而豫廢，兀朮以萬騎馳獵淮上，與顯忠獨立馬圍場間。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liu Yu was deposed; Wuzhu came with ten thousand horsemen to hunt along the Huai, and he and Xianzhong stood alone together in the horse enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was soon deposed; Wuzhu rode ten thousand horses to hunt on the Huai, and he and Xianzhong stood alone together in the riding ring.

sentences.zh: 顯忠戒吳俊往探淮水可度馬處，欲執兀朮歸朝。

translations.literal: Xianzhong instructed Wu Jun to reconnoiter where the Huai could be crossed by horse, intending to seize Wuzhu and bring him back to the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong sent Wu Jun to find a ford on the Huai, planning to seize Wuzhu and bring him back to the Song.

sentences.zh: 俊還，顯忠馳問之，為竹刺傷馬而止。

translations.literal: When Jun returned, Xianzhong galloped to question him; a bamboo spike wounded his horse and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun returned, Xianzhong rode out to meet him, but a bamboo stake lamed his horse and the plan halted.

sentences.zh: 兀朮授顯忠承宣使、知同州。

translations.literal: Wuzhu appointed Xianzhong Chengxuan Shi and made him prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu made him Chengxuan Shi and prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯忠至鄜省侍，永奇教顯忠曰：「同州入南山，乃金人往來驛路，汝可於此擒其酋，渡洛、渭，由商、虢歸朝。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong came to Fu to pay his respects, Yongqi instructed him: "Tongzhou leads into the southern mountains—the Jin courier road. You can seize their chieftain there, cross the Luo and Wei, and return to the dynasty by Shang and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu, Yongqi counseled him: "From Tongzhou into the southern hills runs the Jin courier road—seize their leader there, cross the Luo and Wei, and rejoin the Song through Shang and Guo.

sentences.zh: 第報我知，我當以兵取延安而歸。」

translations.literal: Only inform me when you know; I shall take Yan'an with troops and return."
translations.idiomatic: Send word when you are ready—I will raise troops and recover Yan'an."

sentences.zh: 顯忠赴同州，即遣黃士成等持書由蜀至吳，報歸朝事。

translations.literal: Xianzhong went to Tongzhou and at once sent Huang Shicheng and others with letters through Shu to Wu to report his plan to return to the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong went to Tongzhou and sent Huang Shicheng and others through Shu and Wu with letters announcing his defection.

sentences.zh: 元帥撒里曷來同州，顯忠以計執之，馳出城。

translations.literal: The marshal Salie came to Tongzhou; Xianzhong by stratagem seized him and galloped out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Marshal Salie came to Tongzhou, Xianzhong trapped him by ruse and bolted from the city.

sentences.zh: 至洛河，舟船後期不得渡，與追騎屢戰，皆勝。

translations.literal: At the Luo River the boats were late and he could not cross; he fought repeatedly with pursuing horsemen and always won.
translations.idiomatic: At the Luo the boats were late and he could not cross; he fought off pursuers again and again and always prevailed.

sentences.zh: 顯忠憩高原，望追騎益多，乃與撒里曷折箭為誓，不得殺同州人，不得害我骨肉，皆許之，遂推之下山崖，追兵爭救得免。

translations.literal: Xianzhong rested on the high plain; seeing the pursuers grow ever more numerous, he broke arrows in oath with Salie that he must not kill the people of Tongzhou or harm his kin—all agreed—and then pushed him down the cliff; the pursuers scrambled to save him and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: On the heights, seeing pursuers multiply, he broke arrows with Salie, swearing not to kill Tongzhou people or harm his family; then he pushed Salie off the cliff—the Jin scrambled to save him and he lived.

sentences.zh: 顯忠攜老幼長驅而北，至鄜城縣，急遣人告永奇。

translations.literal: Xianzhong led the old and young on a long dash north to Fucheng County and urgently sent word to Yongqi.
translations.idiomatic: He drove north with the young and old to Fucheng and urgently sent word to Yongqi.

sentences.zh: 永奇即挈家出城，至馬趐穀口，為金人所及，家屬二百口皆遇害。

translations.literal: Yongqi at once took his family out of the city; at Magu Valley mouth they were overtaken by Jurchens and two hundred kin were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqi fled with his family but was caught at Magu Valley; two hundred relatives were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 是日，天昏大雪，延安人聞之皆泣下。

translations.literal: That day the sky was dark and snow heavy; when the people of Yan'an heard of it they all wept.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky darkened and snow fell heavily; all Yan'an wept when they heard.

sentences.zh: 顯忠僅以二十六人奔夏國。

translations.literal: Xianzhong fled to the Xia state with only twenty-six men.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong reached Xia territory with only twenty-six followers.

sentences.zh: 夏人問故。

translations.literal: The Xia people asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia asked his story.

sentences.zh: 顯忠泣，具言父母妻子之亡，切齒疾首，恨不即死，願得二十萬人生擒撒里曷，取陝西五路歸於夏，顯忠亦得報不共戴天之仇。

translations.literal: Xianzhong wept and fully related the deaths of his parents, wife, and children; grinding his teeth and striking his head, he hated that he could not die at once, and wished for two hundred thousand men to capture Salie alive, take the five circuits of Shaanxi for Xia, and himself avenge his mortal foe.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he told how parents, wife, and children had perished; gnashing his teeth, he wished only to die—or to lead two hundred thousand men to seize Salie alive, deliver the five Shaanxi circuits to Xia, and settle his blood feud.

sentences.zh: 夏主曰：「爾能為立功，則不靳借兵。」

translations.literal: The Xia ruler said, "If you can achieve merit in service, I shall not be sparing in lending troops."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia emperor said, "Prove yourself in battle and I will not stint you troops."

sentences.zh: 時有酋豪號「青面夜叉」者，久為夏國患，乃令顯忠圖之。

translations.literal: At that time there was a chieftain styled "Blue-faced Yaksha" who had long been a scourge to Xia; he therefore ordered Xianzhong to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: A chieftain called "Blue-faced Yaksha" had long troubled Xia, and the emperor sent Xianzhong against him.

sentences.zh: 請三千騎，晝夜疾馳，奄至其帳，擒之以歸。

translations.literal: He requested three thousand horsemen, rode day and night, suddenly reached his tent, and seized him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With three thousand horsemen he rode day and night, surprised the camp, and brought him back captive.

sentences.zh: 夏主大悅，即出二十萬騎，以文臣王樞、武臣𠼪訛為陝西招撫使，顯忠為延安招撫使，時紹興九年二月十四日也。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler was greatly pleased and at once sent out two hundred thousand horsemen, appointing the civil official Wang Shu and the military official Ce'e as Shaanxi Pacification Commissioners and Xianzhong as Yan'an Pacification Commissioner—this was on the fourteenth day of the second month of the ninth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Xia emperor sent two hundred thousand horsemen, with Wang Shu and Ce'e as Shaanxi pacification commissioners and Xianzhong as Yan'an commissioner—on the fourteenth day of the second month, Shaoxing year 9.

sentences.zh: 顯忠引兵至延安，總管趙惟清大呼曰：「鄜延路今復歸宋矣，已有赦書。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong led his troops to Yan'an; the superintendent Zhao Weiqing shouted, "The Fuyan circuit has now returned to Song again—there is already an amnesty edict."
translations.idiomatic: At Yan'an Superintendent Zhao Weiqing cried out, "Fuyan is Song again—an amnesty has arrived!"

sentences.zh: 顯忠與官吏觀赦書列拜，顯忠大哭，眾皆哭，百姓哭聲不絕。

translations.literal: Xianzhong and the officials viewed the amnesty edict and bowed in ranks; Xianzhong wept loudly, all wept, and the people's cries of grief did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong and the officials read the amnesty and bowed in ranks; he wept aloud, all wept, and the people's lament never ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃以舊部八百餘騎往見王樞、𠼪訛，諭之曰：「顯忠已得延安府，見講和赦書，招撫可以本部軍歸國。」

translations.literal: He then went with more than eight hundred horsemen of his old command to see Wang Shu and Ce'e and informed them: "Xianzhong has already taken Yan'an Prefecture and seen the peace amnesty; the pacification commissioners may return to the dynasty with their own troops."
translations.idiomatic: With eight hundred veterans he visited Wang Shu and Ce'e: "I hold Yan'an and have seen the peace amnesty—you may return to the Song with your own troops."

sentences.zh: 𠼪訛不從，曰：「初，經略乞兵來取陝西。

translations.literal: Ce'e would not comply and said, "At first the commissioner requested troops to take Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ce'e refused: "The commissioner asked for troops to seize Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 今既到此，乃令我歸耶？」

translations.literal: Now that we have come this far, you tell me to return?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are here, you order us home?"

sentences.zh: 顯忠知勢不可，乃出刀斫𠼪訛，不及，擒王樞縛之。

translations.literal: Xianzhong knew the situation would not yield and drew his blade to hack Ce'e but did not reach him; he seized Wang Shu and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no agreement, he drew his sword at Ce'e but missed, seized Wang Shu, and bound him.

sentences.zh: 夏人以鐵鷂子軍來。

translations.literal: The Xia came with the Iron Hawk army.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia sent the Iron Hawk corps.

sentences.zh: 顯忠以所部拒之，馳揮雙刀，所向披靡，夏兵大潰，殺死蹂踐無慮萬人，獲馬四萬匹。

translations.literal: Xianzhong resisted with his command, galloping and wielding twin blades; wherever he turned the enemy broke; the Xia army collapsed in great rout, killed and trampled without reckoning to ten thousand, and four ten thousand horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He met them with his troops, charging with twin blades; the Xia broke and fled—tens of thousands killed or trampled, forty thousand horses taken.

sentences.zh: 顯忠揭榜招兵，以「紹興九年」為文書。

translations.literal: Xianzhong posted proclamations to recruit troops, using 'the ninth year of Shaoxing' in his documents.
translations.idiomatic: He posted recruitment notices using 'the ninth year of Shaoxing' in the documents.

sentences.zh: 每得一人，予馬一匹，旬日間得萬人，皆驍勇少壯。

translations.literal: For each man gained he gave one horse; within ten days he obtained ten thousand, all fierce, brave, and in their prime.
translations.idiomatic: Each recruit received a horse; in ten days he had ten thousand young warriors.

sentences.zh: 又擒害其父母弟侄者，皆斬於東城之內。

translations.literal: He also seized those who had harmed his parents, brothers, and nephews and beheaded them all within the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: He captured those who had killed his parents and kin and beheaded them in the eastern ward.

sentences.zh: 行至鄜州，已有馬步軍四萬餘。

translations.literal: When he reached Fu Prefecture he already had more than forty thousand horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Fu he commanded more than forty thousand horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 撒里曷在耀州，聞顯忠來，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: Salie was at Yaozhou; hearing Xianzhong was coming, he fled in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: Salie at Yaozhou fled overnight when he heard Xianzhong was coming.

sentences.zh: 四川宣撫吳玠遣張振來撫諭云：「兩國見議和好，不可生事，可量引軍赴行在。」

translations.literal: Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie sent Zhang Zhen to console and instruct him, saying, "The two states are now negotiating peace—do not stir up trouble; you may lead your army in due measure to the imperial residence."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie of Sichuan sent Zhang Zhen with word: "The two courts are making peace—do not provoke trouble; bring your army to the capital when you can."

sentences.zh: 遂至河池縣見玠，玠撫之曰：「忠義歸朝，惟君第一。」

translations.literal: He then went to Hechi County to see Wu Jie; Wu Jie comforted him, saying, "In loyal righteousness returning to the dynasty, you alone are foremost."
translations.idiomatic: At Hechi, Wu Jie received him: "Of all who have returned in loyalty, you stand first."

sentences.zh: 從行使臣崔皋等六百餘人列拜庭下，玠又撫之，犒以銀絹，詣行府受告敕、金帶，除指揮使、承宣使。

translations.literal: More than six hundred attendant envoys including Cui Gao bowed in ranks below the hall; Wu Jie again comforted them, rewarded them with silver and silk, and they went to the pacification office to receive patent edicts and gold belts, being appointed Zhihuishi and Chengxuan Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred followers including Cui Gao bowed in the courtyard; Wu Jie rewarded them with silver and silk, and Xianzhong received patents and a gold belt as Zhihuishi and Chengxuan Shi.

sentences.zh: 至行在，高宗撫勞再三，賜名加賚，又賜田鎮江，以崔皋輩充將佐。

translations.literal: When he reached the imperial residence, Gaozong comforted and rewarded him again and again, granted him a name and additional gifts, also granted him fields in Zhenjiang, and used Cui Gao and his company as his staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: At court Gaozong praised him repeatedly, granted him a name and rich rewards, gave him land in Zhenjiang, and made Cui Gao and the rest his staff.

sentences.zh: 兀朮犯河南，命顯忠為招撫司前軍都統制，與李貴同破靈壁縣。

translations.literal: When Wuzhu invaded Henan, he was ordered as Pacification Bureau vanguard commander-in-chief and together with Li Gui captured Lingbi County.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhu invaded Henan he was made pacification vanguard commander and with Li Gui took Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 兀朮犯合肥，手詔以軍與張俊會。

translations.literal: When Wuzhu invaded Hefei, an imperial autograph ordered his army to join Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhu attacked Hefei, an autograph order sent his troops to join Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 顯忠至孔城鎮，與敵戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Xianzhong reached Kongcheng Town, fought the enemy, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Kongcheng he fought the enemy and routed them.

sentences.zh: 兀朮謂韓常曰：「李世輔歸宋，不曾立功，此人敢勇，宜且避之。」

translations.literal: Wuzhu said to Han Chang, "Li Shifu returned to Song without ever achieving merit; this man is daring and brave—you should for the time being avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu told Han Chang, "Shifu never distinguished himself for Song, but this man is fearless—we should avoid him for now."

sentences.zh: 乃焚廬江而走。

translations.literal: He then burned Lujiang and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He burned Lujiang and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 顯忠欲追之與死戰，俊以奉旨監護，慮失顯忠，遂各以軍還。

translations.literal: Xianzhong wished to pursue and fight to the death; Jun, charged by edict to safeguard him, feared losing Xianzhong, and so each led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong wanted to pursue and fight to the finish, but Jun, under orders to protect him, feared losing him and both armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太后至臨安，顯忠入覲，加保信軍節度使、浙東副總管。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager reached Lin'an, Xianzhong had an audience and was promoted to military commissioner of Baoxin Army and deputy overall commander of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager reached Lin'an he was received in audience and made military commissioner of Baoxin Army and deputy overall commander of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 顯忠熟西邊山川險易，因上恢復策，忤秦檜意。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was thoroughly familiar with the mountains and rivers and their difficulties and advantages on the western frontier; he therefore submitted a plan for recovery, which offended Qin Hui's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the western terrain well, he submitted a recovery plan that offended Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 金使言顯忠私遣人過界，遂降官奉祠，台州居住。

translations.literal: A Jin envoy said Xianzhong had privately sent men across the border; he was therefore demoted, granted temple service, and made to reside in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin envoy accused him of sending agents across the border; he was demoted to temple service and sent to live in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 復甯國軍節度使，升都統制。

translations.literal: He was restored as military commissioner of Ningguo Army and promoted to overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as military commissioner of Ningguo Army and promoted to overall commander.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，金渝盟，詔顯忠以本部捍禦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Jin violated the treaty; an edict ordered Xianzhong to defend with his own command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 the Jin broke the treaty and he was ordered to defend with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 遣統制官韋永壽等以二百騎至安豐軍，與金將小韓將軍兵五千人戰于大人洲，敗之。

translations.literal: He sent the controller Wei Yongshou and others with two hundred horsemen to Anfeng Army; they fought the Jin general Little Han Jiangjun's five thousand men at Daren Islet and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Controller Wei Yongshou with two hundred horsemen to Anfeng; they defeated General Little Han's five thousand at Daren Islet.

sentences.zh: 俄又增兵萬餘來，顯忠率騎軍出，自旦至午，氣百倍，以大刀斫敵陣，敵不能支，殺獲甚眾，掩入淮者不可計。

translations.literal: Soon more than ten thousand additional troops came; Xianzhong led the cavalry out; from dawn to noon their spirit was a hundredfold; with great blades he hacked the enemy formation; the enemy could not stand; kills and captures were very numerous, and those driven into the Huai were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When over ten thousand more arrived he led the cavalry out from dawn to noon, spirit redoubled, hacking the enemy line with great blades until they broke; countless were killed or driven into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 金主亮犯淮西，朝廷命王權拒於合肥。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler Liang invaded western Huai; the court ordered Wang Quan to resist at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Liang of Jin invaded western Huai, the court ordered Wang Quan to hold Hefei.

sentences.zh: 權退保和州，又棄軍渡江，和州失守。

translations.literal: Quan withdrew to defend Hezhou, then again abandoned his army and crossed the river; Hezhou was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Quan fell back to Hezhou, then abandoned his army and crossed the Yangzi; Hezhou fell.

sentences.zh: 金主親統細軍駐和之雞籠山，將濟採石。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler personally led picked troops stationed on Jilong Mountain at He, intending to cross at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor led elite troops to Jilong Mountain at He, preparing to cross at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷詔以顯忠代權，命虞允文趣顯忠交軍，軍中大喜，於是有採石之捷，語在《允文傳》。

translations.literal: The court issued an edict replacing Quan with Xianzhong and ordered Yu Yunwen to urge Xianzhong to hand over the army; the troops rejoiced greatly, and thus came the victory at Caishi—the account is in the Biography of Yunwen.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced Quan with Xianzhong and sent Yu Yunwen to take command; the army rejoiced and won at Caishi—as told in Yunwen's biography.

sentences.zh: 顯忠退軍沙上，得楊存中報：「車駕至平江，可速進兵。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong withdrew his army to the sands and received Yang Cunzhong's report: "The imperial carriage has reached Pingjiang—you may advance troops swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn to the riverbank, he received word from Yang Cunzhong: "The emperor is at Pingjiang—advance at once."

sentences.zh: 顯忠選銳士萬人渡江，盡復淮西州郡。

translations.literal: Xianzhong selected ten thousand elite men, crossed the river, and fully recovered the prefectures and counties of western Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He chose ten thousand elite troops, crossed the Yangzi, and recovered every western Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 軍至橫山澗，與金射雕軍戰，統制頓遇重傷，韋永壽死之，敵兵敗走。

translations.literal: When the army reached Hengshan Ravine they fought the Jin Eagle-shooting army; the controller Dun Yu was gravely wounded and Wei Yongshou was killed, but the enemy troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshan Ravine they fought the Jin Eagle-shooters; Controller Dun Yu was gravely wounded and Wei Yongshou killed, but the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 金主亮切責諸將不用命，諸將弑之而還。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler Liang sharply rebuked the generals for not obeying orders; the generals assassinated him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Liang rebuked his generals for disobedience; they assassinated him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是役也，顯忠所將一萬九千八百六人行賞有差，張振功為最。

translations.literal: In this campaign the nineteen thousand eight hundred and six men under Xianzhong received rewards in varying degrees; Zhang Zhen's merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign his 19,806 men received graded rewards; Zhang Zhen's service ranked highest.

sentences.zh: 詔賜顯忠五子金帶。

translations.literal: An edict granted Xianzhong's five sons gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded gold belts to his five sons.

sentences.zh: 授顯忠淮西制置使、京畿等處招討使，擢太尉、甯國軍節度使、主管侍衛馬軍司公事，赴行在。

translations.literal: He was appointed Western Huai commissioner, Pacification Commissioner for the Capital Region and other places, promoted to Grand Marshal, military commissioner of Ningguo Army, and director of the Palace Guard Horse Bureau, and went to the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Western Huai commissioner and pacification commissioner for the capital region, promoted to Grand Marshal and military commissioner of Ningguo Army, and put in charge of the Palace Guard Horse Bureau before returning to court.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，賜田百頃，兼權池州駐劄御前諸軍都統制，節制軍馬。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne he was granted one hundred qing of fields, concurrently acting as overall commander of the imperial armies stationed at Chizhou, controlling military forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne he received one hundred qing of land and was made acting overall commander of the imperial armies at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，兼淮西招撫使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was additionally made Western Huai Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was also made Western Huai pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時金主褒新立，山東、河北豪傑蜂起，耶律諸種兵數十萬據數郡之地，太行山忠義耿京、王世隆輩皆欲挈地還於朝。

translations.literal: At that time the newly enthroned Jin ruler Bao saw heroes rise in swarms in Shandong and Hebei; Khitan forces of several tens of thousands held several prefectures; on Mount Taihang the loyalists Geng Jing, Wang Shilong, and their kind all wished to bring their territories back to the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The new Jin emperor Bao faced uprisings across Shandong and Hebei; Khitan forces in the tens of thousands held several prefectures; on the Taihang, loyalists Geng Jing and Wang Shilong sought to return their lands to the Song.

sentences.zh: 金懼，亟請和。

translations.literal: The Jin were afraid and urgently sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the Jin urgently sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 顯忠陰結金統軍蕭琦為內應，請出師自宿、亳趨汴，由汴京以通關陝；

translations.literal: Xianzhong secretly allied with the Jin commander-in-chief Xiao Qi as an inside contact and requested to march out from Su and Bo toward Bian, and through the Eastern Capital to open the pass to Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong secretly won over Jin commander Xiao Qi as an inside ally and proposed marching from Su and Bo to Bian, then through Kaifeng to open the road to Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 關陝既通，則鄜延一路熟知顯忠威名，必皆回應，且欲起其舊部曲，可得數萬人，以取河東。

translations.literal: once Shaanxi was connected, the Fuyan route, well acquainted with Xianzhong's martial renown, would surely all respond, and he also wished to raise his old command—he could obtain several tens of thousands of men—to take Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: once Shaanxi was linked, Fuyan—where his name still carried weight—would rally, and he could raise his old followers by the tens of thousands to seize Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時張浚開都督府，四月，命顯忠渡江督戰。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun opened the Grand Marshal's office; in the fourth month Xianzhong was ordered to cross the river and supervise the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had opened the Grand Marshal's office; in the fourth month Xianzhong was ordered across the Yangzi to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 乃自濠梁渡淮，至陡溝，琦背約，用拐子馬來拒，與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Huai from Haoliang to Dougou; Qi broke the agreement and used hooked-horse carts to resist; they fought and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai from Haoliang to Dougou; Qi broke faith and met him with hooked-horse carts, but Xianzhong defeated him.

sentences.zh: 琦復背城列陣，顯忠躬率將士鏖戰，琦敗走，遂復靈壁，入城，宣佈德意，不戮一人，中原歸附者踵接。

translations.literal: Qi again drew up his formation with his back to the city wall; Xianzhong personally led officers and men in fierce battle; Qi was defeated and fled; he then recovered Lingbi, entered the city, proclaimed benevolent intent, and did not kill a single person; those in the central plains who submitted followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Qi made a stand at the walls; Xianzhong led the charge in person, routed him, retook Lingbi, entered the city proclaiming mercy without killing anyone—and the central plains submitted in waves.

sentences.zh: 時邵宏淵圍虹縣未下，顯忠遣靈壁降卒開諭禍福，金貴戚大周仁及蒲察徙穆皆出降。

translations.literal: At that time Shao Hongyuan was besieging Hong County without taking it; Xianzhong sent Lingbi surrendered soldiers to explain fortune and misfortune, and the Jin imperial clansman Da Zhouren and Pucha Tumu all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While Shao Hongyuan besieged Hong County without success, Xianzhong sent Lingbi defectors to preach surrender; the Jin prince Da Zhouren and Pucha Tumu submitted.

sentences.zh: 宏淵恥功不自己出；

translations.literal: Hongyuan was shamed that the merit was not his own;
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan resented that the credit was not his;

sentences.zh: 又有降千戶訴宏淵之卒奪其佩刀，顯忠立斬之，由是二將益不相能。

translations.literal: moreover a surrendered chiliarch complained that Hongyuan's soldiers had seized his sidearm; Xianzhong immediately beheaded the offender, and from this the two generals became even less able to cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: when a surrendered chiliarch complained that Hongyuan's men had stolen his sword, Xianzhong executed the culprit on the spot—and the two generals grew still more hostile.

sentences.zh: 六月，兵傅宿州城，金人來拒，顯忠敗之，斬其左翼都統及首虜數千人，追奔二十餘里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the army invested Suzhou city; the Jurchens came to resist; Xianzhong defeated them, beheaded their left-wing commander-in-chief and several thousand leading captives, and pursued the rout more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he invested Suzhou; the Jin came out to fight and he routed them, beheading their left-wing commander and thousands of captives, pursuing twenty-odd li.

sentences.zh: 宏淵至，謂顯忠曰：「招撫真關西將軍也。」

translations.literal: When Hongyuan arrived he said to Xianzhong, "Pacification Commissioner, you are truly a Guanxi general."
translations.idiomatic: When Hongyuan arrived he told Xianzhong, "Commissioner, you are a true Guanxi warrior."

sentences.zh: 顯忠閉營休士，為攻城計，宏淵等不從。

translations.literal: Xianzhong closed camp to rest the troops and planned for storming the city; Hongyuan and the others would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong closed camp to rest his men and plan the assault; Hongyuan refused to wait.

sentences.zh: 顯忠引麾下楊椿上城，開北門，不逾時拔其城。

translations.literal: Xianzhong led his subordinate Yang Chun up onto the wall, opened the north gate, and within no great time took the city.
translations.idiomatic: He led Yang Chun onto the walls, opened the north gate, and took the city in short order.

sentences.zh: 宏淵等殿后，趣之，乃始渡濠登城。

translations.literal: Hongyuan and the others brought up the rear and urged him on; only then did they first cross the moat and mount the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan's rearguard hurried forward and only then crossed the moat to enter.

sentences.zh: 城中巷戰，又斬首虜數千人，擒八十餘人，遂復宿州。

translations.literal: Street fighting in the city followed; again several thousand heads and captives were cut down and more than eighty men were seized; thus Suzhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Street fighting followed; thousands more were killed or captured and over eighty taken prisoner—and Suzhou was restored.

sentences.zh: 舉寄居官劉時攝州事。

translations.literal: He recommended the sojourning official Liu Shi to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the guest official Liu Shi to administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，授顯忠開府儀同三司、殿前都指揮使，妻周氏封國夫人。

translations.literal: Upon news of the victory he was appointed Xianzhong Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies and commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, and his wife Lady Zhou was enfeoffed as a state lady.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, Xianzhong was made Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies and commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, and his wife Lady Zhou was enfeoffed as state lady.

sentences.zh: 宏淵欲發倉庫犒士卒，顯忠不可，移軍出城，止以見錢犒士，士皆不悅。

translations.literal: Hongyuan wished to open the storehouses to reward the soldiers; Xianzhong would not allow it, moved the army out of the city, and rewarded the men only with cash on hand; the troops were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan wanted to open the granaries to reward the troops; Xianzhong refused, moved the army outside the walls, and paid them only from cash on hand—the men were unhappy.

sentences.zh: 金帥孛撒自南京率步騎十萬來，晨薄城，列大陣。

translations.literal: The Jin commander Besa led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from the Southern Capital at dawn to press the city and deployed a great formation.
translations.idiomatic: Jin commander Besa led one hundred thousand foot and horse from the Southern Capital at dawn against the city in great array.

sentences.zh: 顯忠親帥軍遇于城南，戰數十合，孛撒大敗，遂退走。

translations.literal: Xianzhong personally led the army to meet them south of the city; after several dozen engagements Besa was greatly defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong met them south of the city and after dozens of clashes routed Besa, who fled.

sentences.zh: 統制李福、統領李保各以所部退避，皆斬以徇。

translations.literal: The controllers Li Fu and the commander Li Bao each withdrew with their commands to avoid battle; both were beheaded as examples.
translations.idiomatic: Controllers Li Fu and Li Bao each pulled back with their units; both were beheaded as examples.

sentences.zh: 翼日，敵益兵至。

translations.literal: The next day the enemy brought up more troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day enemy reinforcements arrived.

sentences.zh: 顯忠謂巨集淵並力夾擊，巨集淵按兵不動，顯忠獨與所部力戰百餘合，殺左翼都統及千戶、萬戶，斬首虜五千餘人。

translations.literal: Xianzhong told Hongyuan to strike together from both sides, but Hongyuan held his troops motionless; Xianzhong alone with his command fought fiercely for more than a hundred engagements, killing the left-wing commander-in-chief and chiliarchs and myriarchs and beheading more than five thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong urged Hongyuan to attack from both flanks, but Hongyuan held back; Xianzhong alone fought over a hundred rounds, killing the left-wing commander and many officers and taking more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 俄增兵復來逼城，顯忠用克敵弓射卻之。

translations.literal: Soon more troops came again to press the city; Xianzhong used enemy-subduing bows to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements pressed the city again, he drove them back with powerful bows.

sentences.zh: 宏淵顧眾曰：「當此盛夏，搖扇於清涼猶不堪，況烈日中被甲苦戰乎？」

translations.literal: Hongyuan looked at the troops and said, "In this height of summer, fanning oneself in the cool is still unbearable—how much less fighting in armor under the blazing sun?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan told the men, "In midsummer one can hardly bear a fan in the shade—how can we fight in armor under this sun?"

sentences.zh: 人心遂搖，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Hearts wavered and fighting spirit vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Morale collapsed and the will to fight died.

sentences.zh: 至夜，中軍統制周宏鳴鼓大噪，陽謂敵兵至，與邵世雍、劉侁各以所部兵遁；

translations.literal: At night the central army controller Zhou Hong beat drums and raised a great clamor, pretending the enemy had come; Shao Shiyong, Liu Shen, and each withdrew with their troops;
translations.idiomatic: At night Controller Zhou Hong beat drums and shouted that the enemy was upon them; Shao Shiyong, Liu Shen, and others fled with their troops;

sentences.zh: 繼而統制左士淵、統領李彥孚亦遁。

translations.literal: then the controllers Zuo Shiyuan and the commander Li Yanfu also fled.
translations.idiomatic: then Controllers Zuo Shiyuan and Li Yanfu fled as well.

sentences.zh: 顯忠移軍入城，殿司前軍統制張訓通、馬司統制張師顏、池州統制荔澤、建康統制張淵各遁去。

translations.literal: Xianzhong moved the army into the city; the Palace Front vanguard controller Zhang Xuntong, the Horse Bureau controller Zhang Shiyan, the Chizhou controller Li Ze, and the Jiankang controller Zhang Yuan each fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong withdrew into the city as Zhang Xuntong, Zhang Shiyan, Li Ze, and Zhang Yuan all deserted.

sentences.zh: 金人乘虛復來攻城，顯忠竭力捍禦，斬首虜二千餘人，積屍與羊馬牆平。

translations.literal: The Jurchens seized the opportunity and came again to attack the city; Xianzhong defended with all his strength, beheading more than two thousand captives, corpses piled level with the sheep-and-horse wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin exploited the opening and assaulted the city; Xianzhong held firm, killing more than two thousand—the dead heaped as high as the parapet.

sentences.zh: 城東北角敵兵二十餘人已上百余步，顯忠取軍所執斧斫之，敵始退卻。

translations.literal: At the northeast corner of the city more than twenty enemy soldiers had climbed within a hundred-plus paces; Xianzhong took an axe from the troops and hacked at them until the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When twenty Jin had climbed the northeast wall, he seized an axe and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 顯忠曰：「若使諸軍相與掎角，自城外掩擊，則敵兵可盡，金帥可擒，河南之地指日可復矣。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong said, "If the armies would cooperate in pincer attacks from outside the city, the enemy could be destroyed, the Jin commander captured, and the lands of Henan recovered within days."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If the armies would strike together from outside, we could destroy the enemy, capture the Jin commander, and recover Henan in days."

sentences.zh: 宏淵又言：「金添生兵二十萬來，儻我軍不返，恐不測生變。」

translations.literal: Hongyuan again said, "The Jin have sent two hundred thousand fresh troops; if our army does not return, I fear unforeseen trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan warned, "Two hundred thousand fresh Jin troops are coming—if we do not withdraw, disaster may follow."

sentences.zh: 顯忠知宏淵無固志，勢不可孤立，歎吒曰：「天未欲平中原耶？

translations.literal: Xianzhong knew Hongyuan had no firm resolve and that he could not stand alone; he sighed and exclaimed, "Does Heaven not wish the central plains pacified?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Hongyuan's faint heart and that he stood alone, Xianzhong sighed, "Does Heaven not want the central plains restored?

sentences.zh: 何沮撓若此！」

translations.literal: Why such obstruction!"
translations.idiomatic: Why such obstruction!"

sentences.zh: 是舉，所喪軍資器械殆盡，幸而金不復南。

translations.literal: In this campaign military stores and equipment were nearly all lost; fortunately the Jin did not push south again.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign cost nearly all stores and arms; fortunately the Jin did not advance south again.

sentences.zh: 顯忠以軍還，見浚，納印待罪。

translations.literal: Xianzhong returned with the army, saw Zhang Jun, and surrendered his seal to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew, saw Zhang Jun, and surrendered his seal to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 責授果州團練副使，潭州安置。

translations.literal: He was demoted and appointed deputy military training commissioner of Guozhou, assigned to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Guozhou and exiled to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷知其故，移撫州。

translations.literal: Later the court learned the true cause and moved him to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court later learned the truth and moved him to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道改元，乃還會稽，復防禦使，觀察使、浙東副總管，賜銀三萬兩，絹三萬匹，綿一萬兩。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Qiandao in the first year he returned to Kuaiji, was restored as defense commissioner, made observation commissioner and deputy overall commander of eastern Zhejiang, and granted thirty thousand taels of silver, thirty thousand bolts of silk, and ten thousand taels of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiandao he returned to Kuaiji, was restored as defense and observation commissioner and deputy overall commander of eastern Zhejiang, and granted thirty thousand taels of silver, thirty thousand bolts of silk, and ten thousand taels of cotton.

sentences.zh: 提舉台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: He was made director of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 召除威武軍節度使、左金吾衛上將軍，賜第京師。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed military commissioner of Weiwu Army and upper general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and granted a residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as military commissioner of Weiwu Army and upper general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and given a house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上奇其狀貌魁傑，命繪像閣下。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his imposing stature and ordered his portrait painted in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his imposing frame and ordered his portrait hung in the hall.

sentences.zh: 復太尉。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 乞祠，提舉興國宮，紹興府居住，歲賜米二千石。

translations.literal: He requested temple service and was made director of the Xingguo Palace, residing in Shaoxing, with two thousand shi of grain granted yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He sought temple service, was made director of the Xingguo Palace, lived in Shaoxing, and received two thousand shi of grain yearly.

sentences.zh: 淳熙四年，召赴行在，提舉萬壽觀，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunxi he was summoned to the imperial residence, made director of the Wanshou Abbey, and granted attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi year 4 he was summoned to court, made director of the Wanshou Abbey, and granted attendance.

sentences.zh: 入見，給真奉，賜內庫金，再葺前所賜第賜之，七月卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: On audience he was given true salary, inner treasury gold, and his former granted residence was rebuilt and bestowed again; he died in the seventh month at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he received salary and inner treasury gold; his former house was rebuilt and given again; he died in the seventh month at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡忠襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies and given the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies with the posthumous title Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 楊存中

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong

sentences.zh: 楊存中，本名沂中，字正甫，紹興間賜名存中，代州崞縣人。

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong, original name Yizhong, courtesy name Zhengfu, was granted the name Cunzhong in the Shaoxing era; a native of Guo County in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong, originally Yizhong, courtesy name Zhengfu, received the name Cunzhong under Shaoxing; he was from Guo County in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖宗閔，永興軍路總管，與唐重同守永興，金人陷城，迎戰死之。

translations.literal: His ancestor Min was overall commander of Yongxing Circuit; together with Tang Chong he defended Yongxing; when the Jurchens took the city he met them in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Min was overall commander of Yongxing Circuit; with Tang Chong he defended Yongxing and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 父震，知麟州建甯砦，金人來攻，亦死於難。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was prefect of Lin Prefecture and Jianning Stockade; when the Jurchens attacked he also died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen governed Lin Prefecture and Jianning Stockade and died when the Jin attacked.

sentences.zh: 存中魁梧沈鷙，少警敏，誦書數百言，力能絕人。

translations.literal: Cunzhong was tall, imposing, and taciturn, alert and quick-witted from youth; he could recite several hundred words and his strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong was tall, imposing, and taciturn, sharp from youth, able to recite hundreds of words and stronger than other men.

sentences.zh: 慨然語人曰：「大丈夫當以武功取富貴，焉用俯首為腐儒哉！」

translations.literal: He said to others with feeling, "A great man should win wealth and honor through military achievement—why bow his head to become a pedantic scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: He declared, "A great man wins wealth and honor by arms—why become a pedantic scholar?"

sentences.zh: 於是學孫、吳法，善射騎。

translations.literal: He therefore studied Sunzi and Wuzi methods and excelled at archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Sunzi and Wuzi and mastered archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，山東、河北群盜四起，存中應募擊賊，積功至忠翊郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era bandits rose in swarms in Shandong and Hebei; Cunzhong enlisted to strike bandits and through accumulated merit reached Zhongyi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanhe he enlisted against bandits in Shandong and Hebei and rose to Zhongyi Lang.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，金人再圍汴京，諸道兵勤王，存中與張俊、田師中從信德府守臣梁揚祖以萬兵入援，後隸張俊部曲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang the Jurchens again besieged Bianjing; troops from all routes marched to aid the throne. Cunzhong with Zhang Jun and Tian Shizhong followed Liang Yangzu, defending prefect of Xinde, with ten thousand men into relief, and afterward came under Zhang Jun's command.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang year 1 the Jin again besieged Bianjing; relief armies marched from all routes. Cunzhong followed Zhang Jun and Tian Shizhong under Xinde defender Liang Yangzu with ten thousand men, then served under Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 上問將於俊，俊以存中對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Jun for a general; Jun named Cunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Jun for a general; Jun named Cunzhong.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜袍帶。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was granted robe and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was granted robe and belt.

sentences.zh: 時元帥府草創，存中晝夜扈衛寢幄，不頃刻去側。

translations.literal: When the marshal's headquarters was newly formed, Cunzhong day and night escorted the sleeping quarters and did not leave his side for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the marshal's headquarters was newly formed, Cunzhong guarded the imperial sleeping quarters day and night and never left his side.

sentences.zh: 帝知其忠謹，親信之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his loyalty and prudence and trusted him personally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew his loyalty and prudence and trusted him personally.

sentences.zh: 劇賊李昱據任城，久不克，存中以數騎入，擊殺數百人。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Li Yu held Rencheng and long could not be taken; Cunzhong entered with a few horsemen and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce bandit Li Yu held Rencheng and long could not be taken; Cunzhong entered with a few horsemen and killed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 帝乘高望見，介胄盡赤，意其被重創。

translations.literal: The emperor looked down from on high and saw his armor all red, thinking he had suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Looking down from on high, the emperor saw his armor all red and thought he had been gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 召視之，皆汙賊血，壯之，飲以酒，曰：「酌此血漢。」

translations.literal: Summoned for inspection, it was all bandit blood; impressed, the emperor gave him wine and said, "Drink this—blood of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for inspection, it was all bandit blood; impressed, the emperor gave him wine and said, "Drink this—blood of Han."

sentences.zh: 存中請復往，帝止之。

translations.literal: Cunzhong asked to return; the emperor stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong asked to return; the emperor stopped him.

sentences.zh: 存中曰：「此賊膽碎，即成擒矣。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong said, "This bandit's courage is shattered—he will soon be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong said, "This bandit's courage is shattered—he will soon be taken."

sentences.zh: 遂大破之，復任城，遷閤門祗候。

translations.literal: He then routed them, recovered Rencheng, and was transferred to Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He then routed them, recovered Rencheng, and was made Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，討賊徐明於嘉興，先登。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he attacked the bandit Xu Ming at Jiaxing and was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan year 2 he attacked Xu Ming at Jiaxing and was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 主帥將屠城，存中力諫止之，戮其渠魁而已，郡賴以全。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief was about to massacre the city; Cunzhong strongly remonstrated and stopped it, executing only the ringleaders, and the prefecture was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander meant to massacre the city, Cunzhong stopped him and killed only the ringleaders, saving the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷榮州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，以勝捷軍從張俊守吳門；

translations.literal: When Gaozong crossed south he followed Zhang Jun with the Shengjie Army to defend the Wu Gate;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong crossed south he followed Zhang Jun with the Shengjie Army to defend Wu;

sentences.zh: 苗、劉之變，又從俊赴難。

translations.literal: in the Miao-Liu mutiny he again followed Jun to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: in the Miao-Liu mutiny he again followed Jun into danger.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州團練使，尋為御前右軍統領。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military training commissioner of Guizhou and soon became commander of the Imperial Front Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became military training commissioner of Guizhou and soon commander of the Imperial Front Right Army.

sentences.zh: 金人攻明州，又從俊與田師中、趙密殊死戰，破之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Mingzhou he again followed Jun with Tian Shizhong and Zhao Mi in a fight to the death and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Mingzhou he fought to the death with Jun, Tian Shizhong, and Zhao Mi and won.

sentences.zh: 以奇功遷文州防禦使、御前中軍統制。

translations.literal: For extraordinary merit he was promoted to defense commissioner of Wenzhou and commander of the Imperial Front Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: For extraordinary merit he was made defense commissioner of Wenzhou and commander of the Imperial Front Central Army.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，從俊討李成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he followed Jun to suppress Li Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing he followed Jun against Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 諸將議，多欲分道進，存中曰：「賊勢如此，兵分則力弱，又諸將位均勢敵，非招討督之，必不相為用。」

translations.literal: The generals mostly wished to advance by separate routes; Cunzhong said, "With the bandits' power as it is, dividing the army weakens our force; moreover the generals are equal in rank and power—unless the pacification commissioner directs them, they will surely not act together."
translations.idiomatic: Generals wanted to split forces; Cunzhong said, "With bandits this strong, division weakens us—and equals will not cooperate without the pacification commissioner."

sentences.zh: 俊然之。

translations.literal: Jun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 整軍至豫章，存中率兵數千，首破賊於玉隆觀，追至筠州。

translations.literal: The army reached Yuzhang; Cunzhong led several thousand men and was first to break the bandits at Yulong Abbey, pursuing to Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuzhang, Cunzhong led several thousand men to break the bandits at Yulong Abbey and pursued to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊驍將以眾十萬來援，夾河而營。

translations.literal: A fierce bandit general came with one hundred thousand men in support and camped on both banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce bandit general brought one hundred thousand reinforcements and camped on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 存中謂俊曰：「彼眾我寡，擊之當用奇，願以騎見屬，公以步兵居前。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong said to Jun, "They are many and we few; to strike we must use stratagem—I ask that the cavalry be entrusted to me while you advance the infantry in front."
translations.idiomatic: He told Jun, "They outnumber us—we need a stratagem. Give me the cavalry and advance the foot in front."

sentences.zh: 俊從之。

translations.literal: Jun complied.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 存中夜銜枚渡筠河，出西山，馳下擊賊，俊以步兵夾攻，俘八千人。

translations.literal: Cunzhong at night carried gags in his teeth, crossed the Jun River, came down from the western hills, and charged the bandits; Jun's infantry attacked from both sides and captured eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At night he crossed the Jun River silently, swept down from the western hills, and with Jun's foot on both flanks took eight thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 諸將夜見存中曰：「戰未休，降卒多，忽有變，奈何？

translations.literal: The generals came to Cunzhong at night and said, "The battle is not over and the prisoners are many—if they suddenly revolt, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Generals said at night, "The battle is not over and prisoners are many—if they revolt, what then?

sentences.zh: 非盡殲之不可。」

translations.literal: They must all be killed."
translations.idiomatic: They must all be killed."

sentences.zh: 存中曰：「殺降吾不忍。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong said, "To kill prisoners I cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong said, "I cannot bear to kill prisoners."

sentences.zh: 諸將轉告俊，竟夜坑之。

translations.literal: The generals reported to Jun, and in the end they were buried alive that night.
translations.idiomatic: The generals told Jun, who had them buried alive that night.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追至九江，成遂遁去。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory they pursued to Jiujiang and Cheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Jiujiang, they drove Cheng off.

sentences.zh: 遷宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年春，進神武中軍統制，宰相呂頤浩袖敕以授存中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was advanced to commander of the Divine Martial Central Army; Chancellor Lü Yigao tucked the edict in his sleeve and gave it to Cunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 2 he was made commander of the Divine Martial Central Army; Chancellor Lü Yigao handed him the edict from his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 俊奏留存中軍中，上曰：「宿衛乏帥，朕所選，為不可易也。」

translations.literal: Jun memorialized to retain Cunzhong in the army; the emperor said, "The palace guard lacks a commander—my choice cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked to keep him; the emperor said, "The palace guard lacks a commander—my choice stands."

sentences.zh: 存中亦固辭，且謂：「神武諸帥如韓世忠、張俊，皆貴擁旄鉞，名望至重，如臣麼麼，一旦位與之抗，實不自安。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong also firmly declined, saying, "The Divine Martial commanders such as Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun all nobly bear banners and axes and their fame is very heavy; one such as I, suddenly equal in rank with them, is truly uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong also firmly declined, saying, "The Divine Martial commanders such as Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun all nobly bear banners and axes and their fame is very heavy; one such as I, suddenly equal in rank with them, is truly uneasy."

sentences.zh: 不許，遣中使宣押，乃視事。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; an inner envoy announced his appointment and he took office.
translations.idiomatic: Refused, an inner envoy announced his appointment, and he took office.

sentences.zh: 兼提舉宿衛親兵。

translations.literal: He was additionally made director of the palace guard personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made director of the palace guard personal troops.

sentences.zh: 時中軍卒不滿五千，疲癃者居半。

translations.literal: At that time the central army had fewer than five thousand men, half of them worn out and feeble.
translations.idiomatic: The central army had fewer than five thousand, half unfit for service.

sentences.zh: 存中請拘神武卒借出於外者歸軍中，由是軍政浸修。

translations.literal: Cunzhong requested that Divine Martial soldiers lent outside be recalled to the army, and from this military administration was gradually improved.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled lent-out troops and gradually restored discipline.

sentences.zh: 三年，嚴州妖賊繆羅據白馬源，殺王官，存中討平之。

translations.literal: In the third year the Yanzhou demonic bandit Miao Luo held Baima Pass, killed officials, and Cunzhong suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he suppressed Miao Luo, who held Baima Pass in Yanzhou and had killed officials.

sentences.zh: 除帶禦器械，加保信軍承宣使、權發遣鄜延路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: He was made bearer of the imperial arms, Chengxuan Shi of Baoxin Army, and acting deputy overall commander of Fuyan horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the imperial arms, Chengxuan Shi of Baoxin Army, and acting deputy overall commander of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 六年，為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、密州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made commander of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard and observation commissioner of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he commanded the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard and was observation commissioner of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，張浚視師，謀渡淮以圖劉豫，倚韓世忠為用。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Jun inspected the armies and planned to cross the Huai to strike Liu Yu, relying on Han Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Jun had planned to cross the Huai against Liu Yu, relying on Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 世忠圍淮陽，從浚乞張俊將趙密為助，俊拒之。

translations.literal: Shizhong besieged Huaiyang and begged Jun for Zhang Jun's general Zhao Mi as aid; Jun refused.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong besieged Huaiyang and asked Jun for Zhao Mi; Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎語浚曰：「世忠所欲者趙密爾，存中武勇，不減於密，盍令存中助之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said to Jun, "What Shizhong wants is only Zhao Mi; Cunzhong's martial valor is no less than Mi's—why not send Cunzhong to help?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding told Jun, "Shizhong wants Zhao Mi—Cunzhong is his equal; send Cunzhong instead."

sentences.zh: 浚請於朝，故有是命。

translations.literal: Jun requested this of the court, and therefore came the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Jun so requested, and the appointment followed.

sentences.zh: 於是存中以八隊萬人，趨督府助世忠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cunzhong with eight companies of ten thousand men hurried to the command post to aid Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong took eight companies—ten thousand men—to aid Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 十月，存中與劉猊戰於藕塘，大破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Cunzhong fought Liu Ni at Outang and defeated him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he routed Liu Ni at Outang.

sentences.zh: 猊之初入也，淮西宣撫使劉光世欲棄廬州，退保太平。

translations.literal: When Ni first entered, Western Huai Pacification Commissioner Liu Guangshi wished to abandon Luzhou and withdraw to defend Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Ni invaded, Liu Guangshi wanted to abandon Luzhou for Taiping.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十萬已次濠、壽間，浚命張俊拒之，使存中往泗州與俊合。

translations.literal: The bandit host of one hundred thousand was already between Hao and Shou; Jun ordered Zhang Jun to resist them and sent Cunzhong to Sizhou to join Jun.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thousand bandits stood between Hao and Shou; Jun sent Zhang Jun to resist and Cunzhong to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 及至泗，則光世已舍廬去。

translations.literal: When he reached Sizhou, Guangshi had already abandoned Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou he found Guangshi had already left Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚遣人諭之曰：「一人渡江，即斬以狥。」

translations.literal: Jun sent word: "Whoever crosses the river—behead him as an example."
translations.idiomatic: Jun warned, "Whoever crosses the river will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 光世不得已還廬駐兵，與存中相應。

translations.literal: Guangshi had no choice but to return to Luzhou and encamp, coordinating with Cunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi returned to Luzhou and coordinated with Cunzhong.

sentences.zh: 賊先犯定遠縣，存中以兵二千襲敗於越家坊。

translations.literal: The bandits first attacked Dingyuan County; Cunzhong with two thousand men ambushed and defeated them at Yuejia Lane.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Dingyuan; Cunzhong with two thousand ambushed them at Yuejia Lane.

sentences.zh: 既而與猊兵遇藕塘，賊據山列陣，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Soon he met Ni's troops at Outang; the bandits held the mountain in formation and arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At Outang the bandits held the heights; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 存中急擊之，且使統制吳錫以勁騎五千突其陣。

translations.literal: Cunzhong attacked urgently and had the controller Wu Xi strike the formation with five thousand elite horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong attacked and sent Wu Xi with five thousand elite horse to break the line.

sentences.zh: 陣亂，存中鼓大軍乘之，自以精騎沖其肋，大呼曰：「破賊矣！」

translations.literal: The formation broke up; Cunzhong drummed the great army forward, himself charging the flank with picked horsemen, shouting, "The bandits are broken!"
translations.idiomatic: The line broke; he led the main force in, charged the flank with elite horse, and shouted, "The bandits are broken!"

sentences.zh: 賊錯愕駭視。

translations.literal: The bandits stared in startled dismay.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits stared in dismay.

sentences.zh: 前軍統制張宗顏自泗來，乘背擊之，賊大敗。

translations.literal: The vanguard controller Zhang Zongyan came from Si and struck their rear; the bandits were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyan came from Si and struck their rear; they were routed.

sentences.zh: 猊以首抵謀主李愕曰：「適見髯將軍，銳不可當，果楊殿前也。」

translations.literal: Ni pressed his head to his strategist Li E and said, "I just saw the bearded general—his edge cannot be withstood; it is indeed Yang of the Palace Front."
translations.idiomatic: Ni told his strategist Li E, "That bearded general is Yang of the Palace Front—unstoppable."

sentences.zh: 即以數騎遁去。

translations.literal: He fled with several horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 餘黨萬人僵立失措，存中躍馬叱之，皆怖而降。

translations.literal: The remaining ten thousand stood rigid in confusion; Cunzhong leaped his horse and shouted at them, and all were terrified and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand survivors stood frozen; Cunzhong rode among them shouting, and all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 麟在順昌，孔彥舟方圍光州，聞之皆拔砦遁去，北方大恐。

translations.literal: Lin was at Shunchang and Kong Yanzou was besieging Guangzhou; hearing this both pulled up their stockades and fled, and the north was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin at Shunchang and Kong Yanzou at Guangzhou both fled; the north was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 所得賊舟數百艘，車數千兩。

translations.literal: They obtained several hundred bandit boats and several thousand carts.
translations.idiomatic: They captured hundreds of boats and thousands of carts.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝遣中使勞賜，謂宰執曰：「卿輩始知朕得人也。」

translations.literal: Upon news of the victory the emperor sent an inner envoy to console and reward them, telling the chief ministers, "You now know that I have found my man."
translations.idiomatic: On victory the emperor sent rewards and told his ministers, "Now you see I have found my man."

sentences.zh: 除保成軍節度使、殿前都虞候尋兼領馬步帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Baocheng Army and deputy commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, soon additionally commanding both horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Baocheng Army and deputy commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, soon commanding horse and foot together.

sentences.zh: 存中奏：「祖宗置三衙，鼎列相制，今令臣獨總，非故事也。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong memorialized, "The ancestors established three barracks in tripartite mutual restraint; now to have me command all alone is not precedent."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "The ancestors established three barracks in tripartite mutual restraint; now to have me command all alone is not precedent."

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 七年，為淮南西路制置使，將以撫定酈瓊諸軍，不果行，語在《王德傳》。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Western Huai-An circuit commissioner, intending to pacify the armies of Li Qiong and others, but the plan was not carried out—the account is in the Biography of Wang De.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made Western Huai-An commissioner to pacify Li Qiong's forces, but did not go—as told in Wang De's biography.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to deputy commander-in-chief of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he became deputy commander-in-chief of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 十年，金人叛盟取河南，命存中為淮北宣撫副使，引兵至宿州，以步軍退屯於泗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Jurchens broke the treaty and took Henan; Cunzhong was ordered as deputy pacification commissioner of north Huai and led troops to Suzhou, then withdrew the foot army to encamp at Si.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 the Jin broke the treaty and took Henan; Cunzhong was made deputy north Huai pacification commissioner, advanced to Suzhou, then withdrew the foot to Si.

sentences.zh: 金人詭令來告敵騎數百屯柳子鎮。

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent a false messenger reporting that several hundred enemy horsemen were stationed at Liuzi Town.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent a false report that several hundred enemy horse were at Liuzi Town.

sentences.zh: 存中欲即擊之，或以為不可，存中不聽。

translations.literal: Cunzhong wished to strike at once; some thought it inadvisable, but Cunzhong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong wanted to attack immediately; others dissuaded him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 留王滋、蕭保以千騎守宿，自將五百騎夜襲柳子鎮，黎明，不見敵而還。

translations.literal: He left Wang Zi and Xiao Bao with one thousand horsemen to hold Suzhou and personally led five hundred horsemen in a night raid on Liuzi Town; at dawn, seeing no enemy, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He left Wang Zi and Xiao Bao with one thousand horse at Suzhou and led five hundred in a night raid on Liuzi; at dawn he found no enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 金人以精兵伏歸路，存中知之，遂橫奔而潰。

translations.literal: The Jurchens had elite troops ambush the return route; Cunzhong knew it and fled in disorder crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had ambushed the return route; knowing this, he broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 參議官曹勳不知存中存亡，以聞，朝廷震恐，於是有權宜退保之命。

translations.literal: Participating councilor Cao Xun did not know whether Cunzhong lived or died and reported it; the court was shaken with fear, and therefore came the expedient order to withdraw and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun reported Cunzhong's fate unknown; the court panicked and ordered a precautionary withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 既而存中自壽春渡淮歸泗，人心始安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Cunzhong crossed the Huai from Shouchun and returned to Si, and hearts were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he crossed the Huai from Shouchun to Si and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 冬，引兵還行在。

translations.literal: In winter he led the army back to the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he returned to court with the army.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兀朮恥順昌之敗，復謀來侵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Wuzhu, shamed by the defeat at Shunchang, again plotted invasion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Wuzhu, shamed by Shunchang, plotted another invasion.

sentences.zh: 詔大合兵於淮西以待之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered great concentration of troops in western Huai to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The court massed troops in western Huai to meet them.

sentences.zh: 於是存中以殿司兵三萬卒戍淮，與金人戰於柘皋，敗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cunzhong with thirty thousand Palace Front troops garrisoned the Huai and fought the Jurchens at Zhegao and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong garrisoned the Huai with thirty thousand Palace Front troops and defeated the Jin at Zhegao.

sentences.zh: 時張俊為宣撫使，存中為副使，劉錡為判官，王德為都統制，田師中、張子蓋為統制官。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun was pacification commissioner, Cunzhong deputy commissioner, Liu Qi judge, Wang De overall commander, and Tian Shizhong and Zhang Zigai controllers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was pacification commissioner, Cunzhong deputy, Liu Qi judge, Wang De overall commander, with Tian Shizhong and Zhang Zigai as controllers.

sentences.zh: 金人以拐子馬翼進，存中曰：「敵恃弓矢，吾有以屈之。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens advanced with hooked-horse carts on the wings; Cunzhong said, "The enemy relies on bows and arrows—we have means to bend them."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin advanced with hooked-horse carts on the wings; Cunzhong said, "They rely on bows—we can break them."

sentences.zh: 使萬人操長斧，如牆而進，諸軍鼓噪奮擊，金人大敗，退屯紫金山。

translations.literal: He had ten thousand men wield long axes and advance like a wall; the armies shouted and struck fiercely; the Jurchens were greatly defeated and withdrew to Purple Gold Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent ten thousand men with long axes forward like a wall; the armies shouted and charged; the Jin were routed to Purple Gold Mountain.

sentences.zh: 是役也，失將士九百人，金人死者以萬計，而濠圍猶未解。

translations.literal: In this battle nine hundred officers and men were lost; Jurchen dead were reckoned in the tens of thousands, yet the siege of Hao was still not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hundred Song troops fell; Jin dead numbered in the tens of thousands, but Hao remained besieged.

sentences.zh: 俊與存中、錡先議班師。

translations.literal: Jun with Cunzhong and Qi first discussed withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, Cunzhong, and Qi first discussed withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 會有雲濠路已通者，俊謂錡曰：「吾欲與楊太尉耀兵淮上，安撫濠梁之民，取宣化歸金陵，楊太尉則渡瓜洲還臨安。」

translations.literal: Word came that the Yun-Hao route was open; Jun said to Qi, "I wish to display troops on the Huai with Grand Marshal Yang to reassure the people of Hao and Liang, take Xuanhua and return to Jinling, while Grand Marshal Yang crosses Guazhou back to Lin'an."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Yun-Hao route was open, Jun told Qi, "I wish to display troops on the Huai with Grand Marshal Yang to reassure the people of Hao and Liang, take Xuanhua and return to Jinling, while Grand Marshal Yang crosses Guazhou back to Lin'an."

sentences.zh: 明日，命二帥行。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered the two commanders to march.
translations.idiomatic: The next day both commanders marched.

sentences.zh: 諜報金攻濠甚急，倉皇復回，邀錡會於黃連埠，距濠六十里，聞城陷矣，召存中、錡謀之。

translations.literal: Spies reported the Jin were pressing Hao fiercely; in panic they turned back and met Qi at Huanglian Ford, sixty li from Hao; they heard the city had fallen and summoned Cunzhong and Qi to counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported Hao under heavy attack; they turned back in panic, met Qi sixty li from Hao, learned the city had fallen, and called Cunzhong and Qi to counsel.

sentences.zh: 錡謂存中：「何以處此？」

translations.literal: Qi said to Cunzhong, "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi asked Cunzhong, "What now?"

sentences.zh: 存中曰：「戰爾，相公與太尉在後，存中當居前。」

translations.literal: Cunzhong said, "Fight! The commissioner and Grand Marshal in the rear—I shall take the front."
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong said, "Fight! You and the Grand Marshal hold the rear—I take the front."

sentences.zh: 錡曰：「本來救濠，濠既已失，進無所依，人懷歸心，勝氣已索，此危道也。

translations.literal: Qi said, "We came to save Hao; Hao is lost and advance has no footing; men think of returning and victorious spirit is spent—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "We came to save Hao; it is lost; the men want to go home and spirit is gone—this is perilous.

sentences.zh: 不若退師據險，俟其去，為後圖。」

translations.literal: Better withdraw the army and hold defensible ground, wait until they leave, and plan afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Better withdraw to strong ground, wait for them to leave, and plan again."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「善。」

translations.literal: All the generals said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All the generals said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 鼎足而營，遣人俟敵，曰：「已去矣。」

translations.literal: They camped tripod-fashion and sent men to watch the enemy, who said, "They have gone."
translations.idiomatic: They camped in three divisions and sent scouts to watch the enemy, who said, "They have gone."

sentences.zh: 俊自以為功，謂錡毋往，命存中與德偕至濠。

translations.literal: Jun thought it his achievement and told Qi not to go, ordering Cunzhong and De together to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Jun claimed credit and told Qi to stay, sending Cunzhong and De to Hao.

sentences.zh: 列陣未定，煙起城中，金人伏騎萬餘分兩翼出。

translations.literal: Before the formation was set, smoke rose in the city and more than ten thousand Jurchen hidden horsemen came out on both wings.
translations.idiomatic: Before the line was formed, smoke rose in the city and over ten thousand Jin horse burst out on both wings.

sentences.zh: 存中顧德曰：「何如？」

translations.literal: Cunzhong looked at De and said, "What now?"
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong turned to De: "What now?"

sentences.zh: 德曰：「德小將，焉敢預事？」

translations.literal: De said, "De is a petty officer—how dare he interfere?"
translations.idiomatic: De said, "I am a petty officer—how dare I advise?"

sentences.zh: 存中以策麾軍曰：「那回！」

translations.literal: Cunzhong waved his whip at the army and shouted, "Press back!"
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong waved his whip shouting, "Press back!"

sentences.zh: 諸軍以為令其走也，遂散亂南奔，無復紀律，金人追殺甚眾。

translations.literal: The armies thought he ordered flight and scattered south in disorder without discipline; the Jurchens pursued and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: The troops thought he ordered retreat and fled south in chaos; the Jin pursued and killed many.

sentences.zh: 後一日，韓世忠大軍至，已無及矣。

translations.literal: The next day Han Shizhong's great army arrived—too late.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Han Shizhong arrived—too late.

sentences.zh: 存中乃自宣化渡江歸行在。

translations.literal: Cunzhong then crossed the river from Xuanhua and returned to the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong crossed from Xuanhua to court.

sentences.zh: 加檢校少保、開府儀同三司兼領殿前都指揮使，蓋錄柘皋之功而掩濠梁之敗也。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Junior Guardian, Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Insignia of the Three Excellencies, and additionally commander-in-chief of the Palace Front—recording the merit of Zhegao while masking the defeat at Hao and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Preceptor with the Palace Front command—crediting Zhegao while masking the Hao disaster.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徽宗梓宮攢永固陵，命存中都護。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Huizong's coffin was placed at Yonggu Mausoleum, Cunzhong was ordered to escort it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he escorted Huizong's coffin to Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 竣事，拜少傅，以保傅為管軍自存中始。

translations.literal: When the task was complete he was made Junior Tutor—the first to command armies as guardian tutor began with Cunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When done he was made Junior Tutor—the first guardian-tutor army commander was Cunzhong.

sentences.zh: 十四年，存中請詣太學謁先聖，帝曰：「學校既興，武人亦知崇尚，如漢羽林士皆通《孝經》，況其他乎？」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Cunzhong requested to visit the Imperial Academy to worship the sage; the emperor said, "Now that schools flourish, military men also know to revere learning—as Han Feathered Forest soldiers all studied the Classic of Filial Piety, how much more others?"
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he asked to worship at the Imperial Academy; the emperor said, "Now that schools flourish, military men also know to revere learning—as Han Feathered Forest soldiers all studied the Classic of Filial Piety, how much more others?"

sentences.zh: 二十年，封恭國公。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was made Duke of Gong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，拜少師，恩數視樞密使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was made Junior Preceptor with favors equal to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he was Junior Preceptor with privileges equal to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 存中以凡重地皆有統制官，獨荊、襄無之，請於朝，於是荊南、襄陽初置諸統制。

translations.literal: Cunzhong said that every important post had a controller except Jing and Xiang; he requested it of the court, and thus Jingnan and Xiangyang first established controllers.
translations.idiomatic: He noted Jing and Xiang lacked controllers and secured their establishment.

sentences.zh: 存中在殿嚴凡二十五載，權寵日盛，太常寺主簿李浩、敕令所刪定官陸游、司封員外郎王十朋、殿中侍御史陳俊卿相繼以為言。

translations.literal: Cunzhong in the palace guard for twenty-five years saw power and favor daily grow; Secretariat registrar Li Hao, edict reviewer Lu You, Ministry of Rites outer official Wang Shipeng, and palace censor Chen Junqing spoke in succession.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-five years in the palace guard his power grew; Li Hao, Lu You, Wang Shipeng, and Chen Junqing criticized him in turn.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，罷為太傅、醴泉觀使，進封同安郡王，賜玉帶，朝朔望。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was dismissed as Grand Tutor and director of the Liquan Abbey, advanced to Prince of Tong'an, granted a jade belt, and attendance at the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he was dismissed as Grand Tutor and Liquan director, made Prince of Tong'an with a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 時金主亮有南侵意，存中上備敵十策。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Liang intended southern invasion, Cunzhong submitted ten strategies to prepare against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Liang planned invasion, Cunzhong submitted ten defense strategies.

sentences.zh: 步帥趙密謀奪存中權，因指為喜功生事。
