translations.literal: Foot commander Zhao Mi plotted to seize Cunzhong's power and accused him of seeking merit and stirring trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mi plotted to replace him, accusing him of reckless ambition.

sentences.zh: 存中聞之，上章乞免，密竟代之。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Cunzhong memorialized begging dismissal; Mi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong begged dismissal; Mi replaced him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邊聲日急，九月，詔存中為禦營宿衛使。

translations.literal: Soon the frontier grew urgent; in the ninth month an edict made Cunzhong director of the Imperial Camp guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the frontier alarmed; in the ninth month he was made Imperial Camp guard director.

sentences.zh: 劉汜戰敗於瓜洲，命存中往京口，為守江計。

translations.literal: When Liu Fan was defeated at Guazhou, Cunzhong was ordered to Jingkou to plan river defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Fan's defeat at Guazhou, he was sent to Jingkou to defend the river.

sentences.zh: 虞允文自採石來會，存中與之協力拒敵。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen came from Caishi to join him; Cunzhong coordinated with him to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen came from Caishi; together they held the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵不能濟。

translations.literal: The enemy could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy could not cross.

sentences.zh: 金主亮死，與允文輕舟渡江以伺敵。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Liang died, he and Yunwen crossed the river in light boats to reconnoiter the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Liang died, he and Yunwen crossed in light boats to scout.

sentences.zh: 及金人請和，存中奏俟彼得新主之命，無遽許之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens sought peace, Cunzhong memorialized to wait until they received orders from their new ruler and not hastily agree.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin sought peace, he urged waiting for their new ruler's orders.

sentences.zh: 帝如建康，詔存中扈蹕，因語宰相曰：「楊存中唯命東西，忠無與二，朕之郭子儀也。」

translations.literal: The emperor went to Jiankang and ordered Cunzhong to escort the carriage, telling the chief ministers, "Yang Cunzhong obeys every command east or west; in loyalty none equals him—he is my Guo Ziyi."
translations.idiomatic: At Jiankang the emperor ordered Cunzhong to escort the carriage and told the chief ministers, "Yang Cunzhong obeys every command east or west; in loyalty none equals him—he is my Guo Ziyi."

sentences.zh: 金使復請和，存中請拘之江口，移書審問，若能歸我族屬，還舊壤，損歲幣，復白溝之界，以通兄弟之好，如是則和議可從；

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy again sought peace, Cunzhong requested detaining him at the river mouth and sending letters to inquire: if they would return our kin, restore old territory, reduce yearly tribute, and restore the Baigou border for brotherly relations, then peace could be accepted;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy came again, he proposed detaining him and demanding return of kin, old lands, reduced tribute, and the Baigou border—or execute the envoy and recover by force.

sentences.zh: 不然，請斬其使，亟圖恢復。

translations.literal: otherwise, behead the envoy and urgently plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise behead the envoy and fight.

sentences.zh: 會駕還，以存中為江、淮、荊、襄路宣撫使，給、舍不書黃，命遂寢。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Cunzhong was made pacification commissioner of the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang routes; grant and draft were not written in yellow, and the order lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return he was named pacification commissioner for Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang, but the order lapsed without yellow draft.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仍奉祠。

translations.literal: Soon he was again granted temple service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again granted temple service.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，王師潰于符離，復起存中為御營使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing the imperial army was routed at Fuli; Cunzhong was again raised as Imperial Camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing year 1 the imperial army was routed at Fuli; Cunzhong was again made Imperial Camp commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，金人再入關，議割蜀之和尚原以畀之。

translations.literal: In the second year the Jurchens again entered the passes; there was talk of ceding Sichuan's Heshang Plains to them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the Jin again entered the passes; there was talk of ceding Sichuan's Heshang Plains to them.

sentences.zh: 存中入對，曰：「和尚原，隴右之藩要也。

translations.literal: Cunzhong came for audience and said, "Heshang Plains is a strategic barrier of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong came for audience and said, "Heshang Plains is a strategic barrier of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 敵得之，則可以睥睨漢川；

translations.literal: If the enemy holds it, they can look down on the Han River basin;
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy holds it, they can look down on the Han River basin;

sentences.zh: 我得之，則可以下兵秦雍。

translations.literal: if we hold it, we can move troops down into Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: if we hold it, we can move troops down into Qin and Yong.

sentences.zh: 曩議予金人，吳璘力爭不從。

translations.literal: When surrender to the Jurchens was earlier debated, Wu Lin strongly objected and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When surrender to the Jin was earlier debated, Wu Lin strongly objected and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 今璘在遠，不及知。

translations.literal: Now Lin is far away and does not know of this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lin is far away and does not know of this.

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，非特負陛下，亦有愧於璘。

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak, he will not only fail Your Majesty but also have shame before Lin.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not speak, I will not only fail Your Majesty but also shame Lin.

sentences.zh: 近者，王師盡銳而後得，願毋棄。」

translations.literal: Recently the imperial army exhausted its best troops before regaining it; I beg that it not be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the imperial army exhausted its best troops before regaining it; I beg that it not be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 未幾，金人復攻淮甸，詔存中同都督江、淮事。

translations.literal: Soon the Jurchens again attacked the Huai region; an edict ordered Cunzhong jointly to direct Jiang and Huai affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jin attacked the Huai again; he was ordered to direct Jiang and Huai jointly.

sentences.zh: 湯思退罷，升都督，陛辭，賜坐，賜玉鞍勒。

translations.literal: When Tang Situi was dismissed, Cunzhong was promoted to grand coordinator; at farewell audience he was granted a seat and a jade saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Situi fell, he became grand coordinator and received a jade saddle at audience.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍各守分地，不相統一，存中集諸將調護之。

translations.literal: At that time each army held its own sector without unified command; Cunzhong gathered the generals to coordinate them.
translations.idiomatic: Armies held separate sectors; he gathered generals to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 於是始更相為援。

translations.literal: Only then did they begin to aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did mutual support begin.

sentences.zh: 帝親劄賜之曰：「諸帥協和，互相策應，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote: "The commanders harmonize and respond to one another—your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote, "Commanders now cooperate—your doing."

sentences.zh: 會金兵已深入，朝議欲舍淮保江，存中持不可，乃已。

translations.literal: When Jin troops had penetrated deeply, court opinion wished to abandon the Huai and defend the river; Cunzhong held that this could not be done, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When court opinion favored abandoning the Huai for the river, he objected and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 金兵在揚州，或勸存中擊之。

translations.literal: Jin troops were at Yangzhou; some urged Cunzhong to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: With Jin at Yangzhou, some urged attack.

sentences.zh: 存中不敢渡，獨臨江固壘以老之。

translations.literal: Cunzhong dared not cross; he only faced the river and strengthened ramparts to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not cross, only strengthened river defenses to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 金人尋請盟。

translations.literal: The Jurchens soon sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin soon sought peace.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年班師，加昭慶軍節度使，復奉祠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao the army withdrew; he was made military commissioner of Zhaoqing Army and again granted temple service.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao year 1 the army withdrew; he was made military commissioner of Zhaoqing Army and again granted temple service.

sentences.zh: 時興屯田，存中獻私田在楚州者三萬九千畝。

translations.literal: When military colonies were promoted, Cunzhong presented private fields at Chuzhou totaling thirty-nine thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: When military colonies were promoted, Cunzhong presented thirty-nine thousand mu of private fields at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he died, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 以太師致仕，追封和王，諡「武恭」。

translations.literal: Retired as Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince He with the posthumous title "Wugong."
translations.idiomatic: Retired as Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince He with the posthumous title "Wugong."

sentences.zh: 高宗追念舊臣，為之出涕，賻錢十萬。

translations.literal: Gaozong recalled him as an old minister, shed tears for him, and granted one hundred thousand in funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong recalled him as an old minister, wept for him, and granted one hundred thousand in funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 高宗假借諸將，眷存中尤深，嘗曰：「朕於存中，撫綏之過於子弟。」

translations.literal: Among the generals Gaozong trusted with great leniency, his affection for Cunzhong was deepest; he once said, "In my care of Cunzhong I have treated him more tenderly than my own children."
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals Gaozong indulged, his affection for Cunzhong was deepest; he once said, "In my care of Cunzhong I have treated him more tenderly than my own children."

sentences.zh: 濠、廬之役，親筆戒之曰：「若不便進，當行軍法。」

translations.literal: In the campaigns at Hao and Lu, he personally wrote to warn him, saying, "If advance is inconvenient, military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns at Hao and Lu, he personally wrote to warn him, saying, "If advance is inconvenient, military law will be applied."

sentences.zh: 趙密代領殿帥，則舉唐崔祐甫奪王駕鶴兵權事，豫戒大臣。

translations.literal: When Zhao Mi replaced him as palace guard commander, he cited Tang minister Cui Youfu's stripping Wang Jiahe of military authority and forewarned the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Mi replaced him as palace guard commander, he cited Tang minister Cui Youfu stripping Wang Jiahe of military authority and forewarned the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 及竣事，又曰：「楊存中之罷，朕不安寢者三夕。」

translations.literal: When the matter was concluded, he again said, "At Yang Cunzhong's dismissal I could not rest easy for three nights."
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was concluded, he again said, "At Yang Cunzhong's dismissal I could not rest easy for three nights."

sentences.zh: 存中天資忠孝敢勇，大小二百余戰，身被五十餘創。

translations.literal: Cunzhong by nature was loyal, filial, daring, and brave; in more than two hundred battles large and small he received over fifty wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, filial, and brave, he fought over two hundred battles and took fifty wounds.

sentences.zh: 宿衛出入四十年，最寡過。

translations.literal: In palace guard service for forty years going in and out, he had the fewest faults.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years in the palace guard, he had the fewest faults.

sentences.zh: 孝宗以為舊臣，尤禮異之，常呼郡王而不名。

translations.literal: Xiaozong regarded him as an old minister and treated him with exceptional courtesy, often calling him Prince of the Commandery without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong honored him as an old minister and called him Prince of the Commandery without his name.

sentences.zh: 父、祖及母皆死難，存中既顯，請于朝，宗閔諡忠介，震諡忠毅，賜廟曰顯忠，曰報忠。

translations.literal: His father, grandfather, and mother all died in calamity; once prominent, Cunzhong requested of the court: Min was given the posthumous title Zhongjie, Zhen Zhongyi, and temples were named Xianzhong and Baozhong.
translations.idiomatic: He secured posthumous titles Zhongjie and Zhongyi for his forebears and temples named Xianzhong and Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 又以家廟、祭器為請，遂許祭五世，前所無也。

translations.literal: He also requested a family temple and ritual vessels; thus sacrifice to five generations was permitted—unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: He won permission for a family temple and five-generation sacrifice—unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 祖母劉流落蜀、隴，存中日夜禱祠訪問，間關數千里，卒迎以歸。

translations.literal: His grandmother Liu was lost in Shu and Longyou; Cunzhong prayed and searched day and night, traversing thousands of li in hardship, and at last brought her home.
translations.idiomatic: He searched thousands of li and brought home his grandmother Liu from Shu.

sentences.zh: 禦軍寬而有紀，所用將士，專以才勇選，不私部曲之舊。

translations.literal: He commanded troops with leniency yet discipline, selecting officers for talent and courage alone, not favoring old subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with discipline, choosing officers for talent, not old ties.

sentences.zh: 李顯忠以罪斥，存中奏為統制官，後為名將。

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong was dismissed for a crime; Cunzhong memorialized to make him a controller, and he later became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Li Xianzhong as controller; Li later became a famous general.

sentences.zh: 嘗以克敵弓雖勁而蹶張難，遂以意創馬皇弩，思巧制工，發易中遠，人服其精。

translations.literal: He once said that though enemy-subduing bows were powerful they were hard to draw; he therefore devised the Horse Emperor crossbow, ingeniously made, easy to draw and far-reaching, and men admired its precision.
translations.idiomatic: He devised the Horse Emperor crossbow—easy to draw, far-reaching, and admired.

sentences.zh: 嘗營居鳳山，十年而就，極山川之勝，後獻於朝廷，更築室焉。

translations.literal: He once built a residence on Phoenix Mountain, ten years in the making, surpassing in landscape; later he presented it to the court and built another dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: He built on Phoenix Mountain for ten years, gave it to the court, and built anew.

sentences.zh: 又葺園亭於湖山之間，高宗為書「水月」二字。

translations.literal: He also restored gardens and pavilions between lake and mountain; Gaozong wrote for him the two characters "Water Moon."
translations.idiomatic: He restored lakeside gardens; Gaozong wrote "Water Moon" for him.

sentences.zh: 所居建閣以藏禦書，孝宗題曰「風雲慶會之閣」。

translations.literal: At his residence he built a pavilion to store imperial writings; Xiaozong titled it "Pavilion of Wind and Clouds in Joyous Meeting."
translations.idiomatic: He built a pavilion for imperial writings; Xiaozong titled it "Wind and Clouds in Joyous Meeting."

sentences.zh: 子，偰工部侍郎；

translations.literal: His son Yi was vice minister of the Ministry of Works;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was vice minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 倓簽書樞密院事、昭慶軍節度使。

translations.literal: Tan was signing officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military commissioner of Zhaoqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was signing officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military commissioner of Zhaoqing Army.

sentences.zh: 郭浩，字充道，德順軍隴幹人。

translations.literal: Guo Hao, courtesy name Chongdao, was a native of Longgan in Dejun Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hao, courtesy name Chongdao, was from Longgan in Dejun Army.

sentences.zh: 父任三班奉職。

translations.literal: His father Ren was a third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren was a third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時，充環慶路第五將部將，嘗率百騎抵靈州城下，夏人以千騎追之，浩手斬二騎，以首還。

translations.literal: In the Huizong era he served as a subordinate officer in the fifth command of Huanqing Circuit; he once led one hundred horsemen to the walls of Lingzhou; the Xia pursued with one thousand horsemen; Hao personally cut down two horsemen and returned with their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong he led one hundred horse to Lingzhou; pursued by one thousand Xia horse, he cut down two and returned with their heads.

sentences.zh: 充渭州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He served as military supervisor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was military supervisor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 從種師道進築葺平砦，敵據塞水源，以渴我師，浩率精騎數百奪之。

translations.literal: Following Zhong Shidao in advancing to build Qiping Stockade, the enemy held the pass water source to thirst our army; Hao led several hundred elite horsemen and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Building Qiping Stockade with Zhong Shidao, he seized the pass water source from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵攻石尖山，浩冒陣而前，流矢中左肋，怒不拔，奮力大呼，得賊乃已；

translations.literal: The enemy attacked Shijian Mountain; Hao charged the formation; a stray arrow struck his left rib; in anger he did not pull it out and shouted with all his might until he had the bandit, then stopped;
translations.idiomatic: At Shijian Mountain an arrow struck his left rib; he left it in and fought until he had the enemy;

sentences.zh: 諸軍從之，敵遁去，由是知名。

translations.literal: the armies followed and the enemy fled; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: the armies followed and routed the enemy; his fame began.

sentences.zh: 累遷中州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，進安州團練使。

translations.literal: When Qinzong ascended the throne he was advanced to military training commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qinzong he was military training commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 以種師道薦，召對，奏言：「金人暴露，日久思歸。

translations.literal: On Zhong Shidao's recommendation he was summoned for audience and memorialized, "The Jurchens are exposed in the field; long days make them wish to return.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned on Zhong Shidao's recommendation, he memorialized, "The Jin are exposed in the field; after long days they wish to return.

sentences.zh: 乞給輕兵間道馳滑台，時其半度，可擊也。」

translations.literal: I beg that light troops be given by a secret route to hurry to Huatai—when half have crossed, they can be struck."
translations.idiomatic: Grant light troops by a secret route to Huatai—when half have crossed, strike them."

sentences.zh: 會和戰異議，不能用。

translations.literal: As peace and war were disputed, this could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and war were disputed, and his plan was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝問西事，浩曰：「臣在任已聞警，慮夏人必乘間盜邊，願選將設備。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about western affairs; Hao said, "In my post I already heard alarms; I feared the Xia would seize the interval to raid the border and wished to select generals to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the west, he said, "In my post I already heard alarms; I feared the Xia would seize the interval to raid the border and wished to select generals to prepare."

sentences.zh: 已而果攻涇原路，取西安州、懷德軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they indeed attacked Jingyuan Circuit and took Xi'an Prefecture and Huaide Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they indeed attacked Jingyuan Circuit and took Xi'an Prefecture and Huaide Army.

sentences.zh: 紹聖開拓之地，復盡失之。

translations.literal: The lands opened in the Shaosheng era were again all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng frontier gains were lost again.

sentences.zh: 種師中制置河東，辟以自隨。

translations.literal: Zhong Shizhong was commissioner of Hedong and took Hao on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shizhong took him on his Hedong staff.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，知原州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was made prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyan he was prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，金人取長安，涇州守臣夏大節棄城遁，郡人亦降。

translations.literal: In the second year the Jurchens took Chang'an; the Jingzhou defender Xia Dajie abandoned the city and fled; the prefectural people also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the Jin took Chang'an; Jingzhou's defender fled and the prefecture surrendered.

sentences.zh: 浩適夜半至郡，所將財二百人，得金人不殺，使之還，曰：「為語汝將曰，我郭浩也，欲戰即來決戰。」

translations.literal: Hao happened to arrive at the prefecture at midnight with only two hundred men he led; the Jin did not kill them but sent them back, saying, "Tell your commander: I am Guo Hao; if you wish to fight, come and decide in battle."
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he arrived with two hundred men; the Jin spared them to say, "Tell your commander: I am Guo Hao—come fight if you will."

sentences.zh: 金人遂引去。

translations.literal: The Jurchens then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 升本路兵馬鈐轄、知涇州、權主管鄜延路經略安撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Qianxia of the circuit horse and foot, prefect of Jingzhou, and acting director of Fuyan pacification.
translations.idiomatic: He was made circuit Qianxia, Jingzhou prefect, and acting Fuyan pacification director.

sentences.zh: 時二敵交侵，鄜延之東皆金人，西北即夏境，其屬朝廷者惟保安一軍、德靜一砦。

translations.literal: At that time both enemies invaded; east of Fuyan were all Jurchens and northwest was Xia territory; what remained subject to the court were only Bao'an Army and Dejing Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Both enemies invaded; east of Fuyan was Jin, northwest Xia; only Bao'an Army and Dejing Stockade remained to the court.

sentences.zh: 浩間道之德靜，置司招收散亡，與敵對壘，一年，敵不能犯。

translations.literal: Hao took a bypath to Dejing, established an office to recruit scattered fugitives, confronted the enemy in fortified camps, and for a year the enemy could not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a detour to Dejing, he set up a bureau to gather stragglers and faced the enemy in entrenched camps; for a year they could not break him.

sentences.zh: 再除涇原路兵馬鈐轄、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Military Commander of Jingyuan Circuit and prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Jingyuan circuit Qianxia and Jingzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 浩去，夏人復來，權帥耿友諒僅以身免，一路盡陷。

translations.literal: When Hao left, the Tangut returned; the acting commander Geng Youliang barely escaped with his life, and the whole circuit fell.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, the Xia returned; acting commander Geng Youliang barely escaped, and the entire circuit was lost.

sentences.zh: 張浚為宣撫處置使，以浩為秦鳳路提點刑獄、權經略使、知秦州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, as Pacification Commissioner, appointed Hao Judicial Intendant of Qin-Feng Circuit, acting Pacification Commissioner, and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, as Pacification Commissioner, made him Qin-Feng judicial intendant, acting pacification commissioner, and Qinzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 時浚經略陝西，有言敵可討者，浚意向之。

translations.literal: At that time Jun was directing Shaanxi; some said the enemy could be punished, and Jun inclined toward that view.
translations.idiomatic: While Jun directed Shaanxi, some urged attacking the enemy, and he was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 諸帥恥于不武，莫敢出言。

translations.literal: The commanders were ashamed of appearing unmartial and none dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, ashamed to seem cowardly, dared not object.

sentences.zh: 浚檄五路帥悉所部兵會于富平，浩獨謂敵鋒方銳，且當分守其地，掎角相援，俟釁而動。

translations.literal: Jun ordered the commanders of the five circuits to muster all their troops at Fuiping; Hao alone said the enemy's edge was still sharp and that they should instead divide forces to hold their ground, support one another in pincer fashion, and wait for an opening before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Jun summoned the five-circuit commanders to Fuiping; Hao alone argued the enemy was still sharp, that they should hold their posts in mutual support, and strike only when a gap appeared.

sentences.zh: 浚不聽，師出果敗，五路俱陷，帥府皆徙置他所。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen; the army marched out and was indeed defeated; all five circuits fell, and the headquarters were relocated elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused; the army marched out and was crushed; all five circuits fell and command posts were moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 浚復以浩舊官移知鳳翔府，寓治寶雞縣，又退保和尚原。

translations.literal: Jun again restored Hao to his former rank and transferred him to Fengxiang prefecture, administering from Baoji County, then fell back to defend Heshang Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Jun restored his former rank and moved him to Fengxiang, administering from Baoji, then fell back to Heshang Plains.

sentences.zh: 金人抵原下，浩與吳玠隨方捍禦，蜀以安全。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens reached the foot of the plains, Hao and Wu Jie defended as circumstances required, and Shu remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin reached the plains, he and Wu Jie defended wherever needed, and Shu stayed safe.

sentences.zh: 第功，遷正任防禦使。

translations.literal: By merit he was promoted to a regular commission as Defender-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received a regular appointment as Defender-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，金人破饒風嶺，盜梁、洋，入鳳州，攻和尚原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing the Jurchens broke through Raofeng Ridge, plundered Liang and Yang, entered Feng Prefecture, and attacked Heshang Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 1 the Jin broke through Raofeng Ridge, plundered Liang and Yang, entered Feng Prefecture, and attacked Heshang Plains.

sentences.zh: 浩與吳璘往援，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Hao went with Wu Lin to reinforce them; beheadings and captures numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hao went with Wu Lin to reinforce them; beheadings and captures numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷邠州觀察使，徙知興元府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Bin Prefecture and made prefect of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Bin Prefecture and prefect of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 饑民相聚米倉山為亂，浩討平之。

translations.literal: Starving people gathered on Micang Mountain to rebel; Hao suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people gathered on Micang Mountain to rebel; Hao suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 徙知利州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人以步騎十餘萬破和尚原，進窺川口，抵殺金平，浩與吳玠大破之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens with more than one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry broke Heshang Plains, advanced to reconnoiter Chuankou, reached Shajinping, and Hao with Wu Jie routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin with more than one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry broke Heshang Plains, advanced toward Chuankou, reached Shajinping, and Hao with Wu Jie routed them.

sentences.zh: 遷彰武軍承宣使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chengxuan Shi of Zhangwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chengxuan Shi of Zhangwu Army.

sentences.zh: 玠按本路提點刑獄宋萬年陰與敵境通，利所鞫不同，由是與浩意不協，朝廷乃徙浩知金州兼永興軍路經略使。

translations.literal: When Jie investigated circuit judicial intendant Song Wannian's secret communications with enemy territory, Lizhou's inquest differed, and from this he and Hao were not in agreement; the court thereupon transferred Hao to be prefect of Jin Prefecture and concurrently pacification commissioner of Yongxing Army Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie investigated circuit judicial intendant Song Wannian's secret communications with enemy territory, Lizhou's inquest differed; he and Hao fell out, and the court transferred Hao to Jin Prefecture and Yongxing Army Circuit pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 金州殘弊特甚，戶口無幾，浩招輯流亡，開營田，以其規置頒示諸路。

translations.literal: Jinzhou was especially devastated, with scarcely any households left; Hao gathered exiles, opened military colonies, and circulated his arrangements to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou was ruinously depopulated; he gathered refugees, opened military farms, and published his system to other circuits.

sentences.zh: 他軍以匱急仰給朝廷，浩獨積贏錢十萬緡以助戶部，朝廷嘉之，凡有奏請，得以直達。

translations.literal: Other armies, straitened, relied on the court for supplies; Hao alone accumulated a surplus of one hundred thousand strings of cash to assist the Ministry of Revenue; the court praised him, and whatever he memorialized could go straight to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Other armies begged the court for funds; he alone amassed a surplus of 100,000 strings for the Ministry of Revenue, won praise, and his memorials went directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 九年，改金、洋、房州節制。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was reassigned to command Jin, Yang, and Fang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was made commander of Jin, Yang, and Fang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 金人還河南地，以浩為龍、神衛四廂都指揮使，充陝西宣諭使、知金州。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens returned the Henan territories, Hao was made Commander of the Four Bureaus of the Dragon and Spirit Guards, Shaanxi Pacification Envoy, and prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin returned Henan, he became Dragon and Spirit Guard commander, Shaanxi envoy, and Jinzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 樓炤行關中，辟浩樞密院都統制、節制陝西軍馬。

translations.literal: When Lou Zhao toured Guanzhong, he recruited Hao as Director-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Commander of Shaanxi forces.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao, touring Guanzhong, appointed him Bureau Director-in-chief and commander of Shaanxi forces.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made Fengguo military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五路陷，徙知夔州，未行，移知金州，仍永興路經略安撫使、節制陝西河東兼措置河東路忠義軍馬。

translations.literal: When the five circuits fell he was transferred to Kuizhou; before he departed he was moved to Jinzhou, still Pacification Commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, commanding Shaanxi and Hedong and arranging the loyalist forces of the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the five circuits fell he was posted to Kuizhou, then reassigned to Jinzhou before leaving, still Yongxing pacification commissioner, commanding Shaanxi and Hedong and organizing Hedong loyalist troops.

sentences.zh: 十一年，金人內侵，宣撫使胡世將召浩及吳璘、楊政會仙人原，授以攻取之策。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Jurchens invaded inland; the Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang summoned Hao, Wu Lin, and Yang Zheng to Xianren Plains and gave them plans to attack and recover territory.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the Jin invaded inland; Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang summoned Hao, Wu Lin, and Yang Zheng to Xianren Plains with plans to strike back.

sentences.zh: 浩遺裨將設伏破之。

translations.literal: Hao sent a lieutenant to set an ambush and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent a lieutenant with an ambush and routed them.

sentences.zh: 十四年，召見，拜檢校少保，還鎮，賜以禦府金器、繡鞍，仍官一子文資，賜田五十頃。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned to audience, made Junior Guardian, and returned to his command; he was given imperial gold vessels and an embroidered saddle, one son was granted a civil post, and fifty qing of land were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was summoned, made Junior Guardian, and returned to command with imperial gold, an embroidered saddle, a civil post for one son, and fifty qing of land.

sentences.zh: 浩辭曰：「臣父子起身行陣，不敢忘本，願還文資。」

translations.literal: Hao declined, saying, "My father and I rose from the ranks and dare not forget our origins; I beg to return the civil post."
translations.idiomatic: Hao declined: "My father and I rose from the ranks and dare not forget our origins; please take back the civil post."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，別與一子閣職。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his intent and separately granted another son a palace post.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and gave another son a palace appointment instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲，分利州為東西兩路，以浩為金房開達州經略安撫使兼知金州、樞密院都統制，屯金州，仍建帥府。

translations.literal: That year Lizhou was divided into eastern and western circuits; Hao was made Pacification Commissioner of Jin, Fang, and Kaida prefectures while also prefect of Jinzhou and Director-in-chief of the Bureau, garrisoned at Jinzhou, and a headquarters was established.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lizhou was split east and west; he became pacification commissioner of Jin, Fang, and Kaida, Jinzhou prefect, and Bureau Director-in-chief, garrisoned at Jinzhou with a new headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈檢校少帥，諡恭毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Marshal; his posthumous title was Respectful and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Junior Marshal with the posthumous name Respectful and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，賜立廟金州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi a temple was granted at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunxi a temple was established for him at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊政，字直夫，原州臨涇人。

translations.literal: Yang Zheng, style Zhifu, was a native of Lingjing in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zheng, styled Zhifu, was from Lingjing in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇甯三年，夏人舉國大入，父忠戰歿，政甫七歲，哀號如成人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning the Tangut invaded on a national scale; his father Zhong died in battle; Zheng was only seven years old and wailed like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning year 3 the Xia invaded in force; his father Zhong fell in battle when Zheng was only seven, yet he wailed like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 其母奇之，曰：「孝於親者必忠於君，此兒其大吾門乎？」

translations.literal: His mother marveled at this and said, "One filial to parents will be loyal to his lord—will this child enlarge our house?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother was struck by it: "Filial sons prove loyal ministers—will this boy enlarge our clan?"

sentences.zh: 宣和末，應募為弓箭手。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era he enlisted as an archer.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanhe he enlisted as an archer.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，因拒夏人，稍知名。

translations.literal: In the early Jingkang period, by resisting the Tangut he became slightly known.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingkang he won notice by resisting the Xia.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，從吳玠擊金人，九戰九捷。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era he followed Wu Jie in fighting the Jurchens and won nine battles in nine engagements.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyan years he followed Wu Jie against the Jin and won nine straight victories.

sentences.zh: 累功至武顯郎。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he rose to Wuxianlang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit raised him to Wuxianlang.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年春，金人趨和尚原，又攻箭筈關，政引兵大破之，斬千戶一、酋長二。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Shaoxing the Jurchens pressed toward Heshang Plains and also attacked Jian'guan Pass; Zheng led troops and routed them, beheading one chiliarch and two chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing spring the Jin pressed Heshang Plains and attacked Jian'guan Pass; Zheng routed them, beheading one chiliarch and two chieftains.

sentences.zh: 遷右武大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Martial Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Martial Grandee.

sentences.zh: 十月，金兵大集，號十萬，自寶雞列柵至原下。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Jurchen army massed, claiming one hundred thousand men, and from Baoji erected palisades down to the foot of the plains.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Jin massed, claiming 100,000 men, and palisaded from Baoji to the foot of the plains.

sentences.zh: 吳玠與相持累日，以政統領將兵迎敵，日數十合，士卒無不一當百。

translations.literal: Wu Jie held them for many days and had Zheng lead the troops to meet the enemy; there were dozens of clashes daily, and not one soldier failed to fight as if worth a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie held them for days while Zheng led the vanguard in dozens of daily clashes; every man fought as ten.

sentences.zh: 復出奇兵斷其糧道，敵少卻，遮擊之，獲萬戶及首領三百余人、甲士八百六十人。

translations.literal: He again sent an ambush to cut their supply route; when the enemy fell back slightly he intercepted them and captured more than three hundred myriarchs and chieftains and eight hundred sixty armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He again ambushed their supply line; when they slackened he struck and took 300+ officers including myriarchs and 860 armored troops.

sentences.zh: 拜恭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gongzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 時有嫉政者，以母妻尚留北境，不宜屬以兵權，玠不聽，政益感奮。

translations.literal: At the time some who envied Zheng said that because his mother and wife still remained in the northern territories he ought not be entrusted with military authority; Jie would not listen, and Zheng was all the more inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Envious rivals said his mother and wife still in the north disqualified him for command; Jie ignored them, and Zheng fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 二年，金合步騎數千柵魚龍川口，政帥精兵劫破之。

translations.literal: In the second year the Jurchens combined infantry and cavalry in the thousands and palisaded the mouth of Yulong River; Zheng led elite troops in a raid and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the Jin massed thousands of horse and foot at Yulong River mouth; Zheng's elite raiders smashed them.

sentences.zh: 升隴州團練使，移知方山原，軍儲芻穀在其中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regimental Trainer of Longzhou and transferred to Fangshan Plains, where army grain and fodder were stored.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Longzhou regimental trainer, he was moved to Fangshan Plains, the depot for army grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 三月，金大軍來攻，城且下，政擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the third month a great Jurchen army came to attack; the city was nearly taken, but Zheng defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month a great Jin army attacked; the city nearly fell before Zheng beat them back.

sentences.zh: 選知鳳州。

translations.literal: He was selected as prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，金攻饒風關，政從玠戰關下，凡六日。

translations.literal: In the third year the Jurchens attacked Raofeng Pass; Zheng followed Jie in fighting below the pass for six days in all.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the Jin attacked Raofeng Pass; Zheng fought six days under Jie at the pass.

sentences.zh: 改明州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was made Observer of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Mingzhou observer.

sentences.zh: 四年，撒離喝裒精兵十萬，欲道仙人關入蜀，至上奢田。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wanyan Zonghan gathered one hundred thousand elite troops, intending to enter Shu by way of Xianren Pass, and reached Shangshe field.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Wanyan Zonghan massed 100,000 elite troops to enter Shu via Xianren Pass and reached Shangshe.

sentences.zh: 玠築壘於關外，政曰：「此地為蜀厄塞，當堅守，時出奇擊之。」

translations.literal: Jie built ramparts outside the pass; Zheng said, "This place is the chokepoint of Shu and must be held firmly, with occasional surprise strikes."
translations.idiomatic: Jie fortified outside the pass; Zheng said, "This is Shu's vital gate—hold it firm and strike when chances appear."

sentences.zh: 玠用其言。

translations.literal: Jie adopted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jie followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 金人變態多端，政隨機應之，連日百余戰。

translations.literal: The Jurchens varied their tactics in many ways; Zheng responded as circumstances required, and for successive days there were more than a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin shifted tactics endlessly; Zheng adapted, fighting more than a hundred engagements in successive days.

sentences.zh: 敵帥督戰益急，政命卒以神臂弓射之；

translations.literal: As the enemy commander pressed the battle ever harder, Zheng ordered his soldiers to shoot him with divine-arm bows;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy commander pressed hardest, Zheng had his men shoot him with divine-arm bows;

sentences.zh: 又選甲士千餘出山谷，斷其兵，使不得進退；

translations.literal: he also chose more than a thousand armored men to emerge from the valleys, cut off the enemy troops, and prevent advance or retreat;
translations.idiomatic: then sent 1,000+ armored men from the valleys to cut the enemy column and trap them;

sentences.zh: 又出敵不意，夜斫其營。

translations.literal: and again, catching them unawares, he hacked their camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: and by night struck their camp where they did not expect it.

sentences.zh: 敵遂遁去，追至河池而還。

translations.literal: The enemy then fled; he pursued to Hechi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled; he pursued to Hechi and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 授龍神衛四廂都指揮使、環慶路經略安撫使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander of the Four Bureaus of the Dragon and Spirit Guards and Pacification Commissioner of Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Dragon and Spirit Guard commander and Huanqing pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，金人攻淮，玠命政帥師乘機牽制，至秦州，一戰而拔，撫定居民，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Jurchens attacked the Huai region, Jie ordered Zheng to lead troops and seize the moment to pin them down; reaching Qinzhou, he took it in a single battle, pacified the inhabitants, and harmed not a hair.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, when the Jin attacked the Huai, Jie ordered Zheng to pin them down; at Qinzhou he took the city in one fight, pacified the people, and harmed none.

sentences.zh: 改經略安撫涇原兼帥環慶、利路。

translations.literal: He was changed to Pacification Commissioner of Jingyuan while also commanding Huanqing and the Li circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jingyuan pacification commissioner while also commanding Huanqing and Li circuits.

sentences.zh: 三鎮事叢集，剖決無滯。

translations.literal: Affairs of the three garrisons piled up together, yet he decided them without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Business from three commands piled up, yet he decided every case without backlog.

sentences.zh: 母留敵境，間遣人省視之，母惟勉以忠義。

translations.literal: His mother remained in enemy territory; he occasionally sent people to visit her, and she only exhorted him with loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His mother stayed behind enemy lines; he sometimes sent visitors, and she urged only loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 九年春，和議成，始得迎母及兄弟歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, when the peace treaty was concluded, he was at last able to welcome his mother and brothers home.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 9, once peace was made, he finally brought his mother and brothers home.

sentences.zh: 乞祠以便養，不許。

translations.literal: He requested a temple post to care for her, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a temple appointment to nurse her, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 詔封其母感義郡夫人，以政為熙河蘭鞏路經略安撫使、知熙州，進武康軍承宣使。

translations.literal: An edict ennobled his mother as Lady of the Ganyi Commandery; Zheng was made Pacification Commissioner of the Xihe-Lan-Gong circuit and prefect of Xizhou, and promoted to Commissioner of the Wukang Army.
translations.idiomatic: The court ennobled his mother Lady Ganyi, made him Xihe-Lan-Gong pacification commissioner and Xizhou prefect, and promoted him to Wukang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙利州，又徙興元。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Lizhou, then again to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was moved to Lizhou, then to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 會金人渝盟，政建迎敵之策，兼川、陝宣撫副使司都統制。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens violated the treaty, Zheng drew up a plan to meet the enemy and was also made Director-in-chief under the Sichuan-Shaanxi Deputy Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty, he drafted a counterattack plan and became director-in-chief under the Sichuan-Shaanxi deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 政偕統制楊從義劫金人於鳳翔府城南砦，敗之，獲戰馬數百。

translations.literal: Zheng together with the Director Yang Congyi raided the Jurchens at the southern stockade outside Fengxiang prefecture, defeated them, and captured several hundred war horses.
translations.idiomatic: With Director Yang Congyi he raided the Jin at Fengxiang's southern stockade, routed them, and seized hundreds of horses.

sentences.zh: 母卒，起復，遂帥師趣寶雞渭水上，以拒敵沖，凡大戰七，斬獲甚多。

translations.literal: When his mother died he resumed office from mourning, then led his army to the Wei River above Baoji to block the enemy's thrust; there were seven great battles in all, with many beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left mourning to lead troops to the Wei above Baoji, blocking the enemy in seven major battles with heavy kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 川、陝宣撫副使胡世將奏：「鳳翔之捷，政奮不顧身，功效顯著。」

translations.literal: The Sichuan-Shaanxi Deputy Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang memorialized: "In the victory at Fengxiang, Zheng fought recklessly of his own life and his achievement was conspicuous."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang reported: "At Fengxiang, Zheng risked his life with conspicuous merit."

sentences.zh: 拜武當軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was made Military Commissioner of the Wudang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Wudang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，金將胡盞、習不祝合軍五萬來攻，政與吳璘、郭浩會于仙人原。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year the Jurchen generals Hu Khan and Xiebuzhu combined fifty thousand troops to attack; Zheng met Wu Lin and Guo Hao at Xianren Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year 11 Jin generals Hu Khan and Xiebuzhu attacked with 50,000 men; Zheng joined Wu Lin and Guo Hao at Xianren Plains.

sentences.zh: 世將授以攻取之策，政出和尚原，浩出商州以為援，璘駐秦州。

translations.literal: Shijiang gave them plans to attack and recover territory: Zheng was to advance from Heshang Plains, Hao from Shangzhou as relief, and Lin to hold Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shijiang gave the attack plan: Zheng from Heshang Plains, Hao from Shangzhou in support, Lin garrisoning Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 政引兵夜入隴州界，遂趨吳山，與金人對壘，又敗金萬戶通檢於寶雞。

translations.literal: Zheng led his troops by night into Longzhou territory, then hurried to Wushan and faced the Jurchens in fortified camps; he again defeated the Jurchen myriarch Tongjian at Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng marched by night into Longzhou, rushed to Wushan to face the Jin in camp, and again defeated myriarch Tongjian at Baoji.

sentences.zh: 時通檢居渭北，政欲攻拔其城，通檢將精甲萬眾出，政帥勇士鏖戰，遣裨將突出陣後，登山執幟。

translations.literal: At that time Tongjian was north of the Wei; Zheng wished to storm his city, but Tongjian led ten thousand elite armored men out; Zheng led his warriors in fierce combat and sent a lieutenant to burst out behind the formation, climb the hill, and raise banners.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian held the north bank; Zheng tried to take his city, but Tongjian led 10,000 elite armored troops out; Zheng fought fiercely while a lieutenant circled behind, climbed the hill, and raised banners.

sentences.zh: 金軍見之，大呼曰：「伏發矣！」

translations.literal: The Jurchen army saw this and shouted, "The ambush has sprung!"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin saw the banners and cried, "Ambush!"

sentences.zh: 乃驚潰。

translations.literal: They then panicked and routed.
translations.idiomatic: They panicked and broke.

sentences.zh: 政乘勝掩殺，通檢走至城門而橋已絕，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Zheng pressed the victory in pursuit; Tongjian fled to the city gate, but the bridge was already cut, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng pursued; Tongjian reached the gate, found the bridge gone, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 和議成，帝召政還，軍民詣部使者借留。

translations.literal: When the peace treaty was concluded the Emperor summoned Zheng back, but soldiers and civilians went to the circuit commissioner to beg that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: After peace the Emperor recalled him, but troops and civilians begged the commissioner to keep him.

sentences.zh: 及入見，條奏詳明，帝善之。

translations.literal: When he entered audience his memorials were detailed and clear, and the Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At court his reports were lucid and thorough, and the Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 十三年，還鎮，加檢校少保，賜田五十頃。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he returned to his command, was given the additional title Junior Guardian, and was granted fifty qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he returned to command, was made Junior Guardian, and received fifty qing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，分利州為東西兩路，政屯興元府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Lizhou was divided into eastern and western circuits, and Zheng garrisoned Xingyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Lizhou was split east and west, and Zheng garrisoned Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太尉。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous title was Accomplished and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor with Three Excellencies honors, posthumous name Accomplished and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 政守漢中十八年，六堰久壞，失灌溉之利，政為修復。

translations.literal: Zheng held Hanzhong for eighteen years; the six weirs had long been ruined and irrigation lost, and he restored them.
translations.idiomatic: For eighteen years at Hanzhong he restored six ruined weirs that had long ceased to irrigate the fields.

sentences.zh: 漢江水決為害，政築長堤捍之。

translations.literal: When the Han River burst its banks to do harm, Zheng built a long dike to hold it back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han burst its banks he built a long dike to contain it.

sentences.zh: 凡利於民者不敢以軍旅廢。

translations.literal: Whatever benefited the people he did not abandon because of military duties.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever helped the people he never set aside for campaigning.

sentences.zh: 休兵十餘年，未嘗升遷將士，上下安之。

translations.literal: For more than ten years of peace he never promoted officers or soldiers, yet superiors and subordinates were content.
translations.idiomatic: Through more than ten years of peace he promoted no one, yet officers and men were content.

sentences.zh: 政故為吳璘裨將，及與璘分道建帥，執門下之禮益恭，世頗賢之。

translations.literal: Zheng had formerly been Wu Lin's lieutenant; when they later held separate commands he observed even more scrupulously the courtesy due a subordinate at the gate, and the age widely admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Lin's lieutenant, he later held a separate command yet showed even greater deference as a former subordinate—a conduct widely admired.

sentences.zh: 論曰：李顯忠生而神奇，立功異域，父子破家狥國，志復中原，中罹讒構，屢遭廢黜，傷哉！

translations.literal: The commentary says: Li Xianzhong was born marvelous, achieved merit in foreign lands, and father and son ruined their house to die for the state with the aim of restoring the Central Plains; yet midway he suffered slander and was repeatedly dismissed—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Li Xianzhong seemed marked from birth, won glory abroad, and father and son ruined themselves for the state to recover the Central Plains—yet slander drove him from office again and again. Alas!

sentences.zh: 楊存中出入淮甸，無大勝負，典兵最久，貴寵獨隆，然頗能知幾，不阽禍敗，其亦有天幸者歟？

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong moved in and out of the Huai region with no great victories or defeats; he commanded troops longest and enjoyed favor alone supreme, yet he could rather perceive the moment and did not verge on disaster—did he also have Heaven's fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong shuttled the Huai with no great wins or losses, commanded longest, and stood alone in favor—yet he read the times and never courted ruin. Was that fortune as well?

sentences.zh: 郭浩、楊政克左右，玠、璘兄弟保全川蜀。

translations.literal: Guo Hao and Yang Zheng were at his left and right; the brothers Wu Jie and Wu Lin preserved Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hao and Yang Zheng flanked them; the brothers Jie and Lin held Shu.

sentences.zh: 數君子皆人所屬倚以成功者，奈何撓於和議，頻失事機，人心沮喪，不得如吉甫、方叔，受祉振旅以成中興之業，惜哉！

translations.literal: These several gentlemen were all men on whom people relied for success—yet how were they hampered by the peace talks, repeatedly missing their chance, hearts disheartened, unable like Jifu and Fangshu to receive blessings and marshal the armies to complete the work of restoration? How regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: These were the men the realm trusted for victory—yet peace talks thwarted them, chances slipped away, spirits sank, and unlike the classic ministers Jifu and Fangshu they could not receive Heaven's blessing, rouse the hosts, and finish the restoration. A pity!
